pattern.type: speckled / granite
pattern.speckle_description: dense salt-and-pepper mineral grains of white, blue-grey, black, and warm brown across the surface

ALASKA WHITE.visual_description: A busy granite with a white base densely packed with mineral speckling in blue-grey, black, and warm brown crystals. Distinctive blue crystal accents give it a subtle cool glow. Overall a 'stone with texture' — grainy salt-and-pepper rather than veined marble. Very different from every other stone in the Whites family because it is a granite, not a marble or quartzite.
ALASKA WHITE.differentiator: The only granite in the Whites family — uniform speckled texture with mineral grains instead of veining. Within Whites, if asked 'which white has no veins and looks grainy/busy,' it is Alaska White. Distinguished from every marble white (Thassos, Statuario, Bianco Lasa, etc.) by its crystalline granite structure and multi-color speckling.

pattern.type: cream-white crystalline field with warm gold diagonal linear veining
pattern.vein_color: warm gold, grey crystalline, occasional fine white

ALGAE VITRUM.visual_description: A cream-white quartzite with warm gold diagonal linear veining running across the slab and scattered grey crystalline clusters. NOT pink or red despite the folder grouping — the stone reads as a warm-white quartzite. One rep had a Stonex label reading 'SEASON BLUE' suggesting possible folder/trade-name confusion. Needs inventory review.
ALGAE VITRUM.differentiator: Cream-white quartzite with diagonal gold veining — NOT pink/red. Likely trade-name confusion at inventory level. Closer to White quartzites than any Pinks/Reds stone.

color.accent: fine white crackle veins and warm gold filaments

pattern.type: salmon-pink flows with cream-white cloudy zones and white crackle veining
pattern.vein_color: fine white, warm gold, darker rose shadows
pattern.vein_density: medium — full-coverage flowing pattern with crackle accents

AMAZON BLUSH.visual_description: A salmon-pink / dusty rose Brazilian quartzite with sweeping cream-white cloudy zones and a network of fine white crackle veins threaded with warm gold filaments. Despite the 'Amazon' name (which suggests green), visually this is a distinct pink stone — user-confirmed for Pinks/Reds family.
AMAZON BLUSH.differentiator: Salmon-pink with cream clouds and white crackle — warmer and cloudier than Valle Rossa (pale rose quartzite), less crackled than Pink Valencia (saturated marble crackle). Brazilian quartzite body (crystalline) distinguishes it from marble pinks.

color.accent: rust-brown and pink feldspar inclusions at cell edges

pattern.type: large polygonal mosaic cells of turquoise with darker mineral edges
pattern.vein_color: darker teal, rust-brown, pink feldspar at cell boundaries
pattern.vein_thickness: thin edge-lines between large polygonal cells
pattern.vein_density: medium — cell boundaries define the pattern; cells themselves are uniformly turquoise

AMAZONITE.visual_description: A vibrant turquoise-green semi-precious stone slab composed of large polygonal mosaic-like cells, each a saturated turquoise-green, separated by darker teal mineral edges and occasional rust-brown and pink feldspar inclusions. The effect is almost like crazy-paving tiles in turquoise — a distinctive tessellated mosaic look. Near-identical twin with Amozonita.
AMAZONITE.differentiator: Near-identical sister stone to Amozonita — BOTH are turquoise semi-precious stones with the same family-level look. Amazonite tends to show more UNIFORM turquoise cells with crisp dark edges (mosaic feel); Amozonita tends to show patchier turquoise clusters against more visible white crystalline matrix (the turquoise is present in large patches, not uniform cells). Physical side-by-side needed to call reliably. NOT similar to Aqua Patagonia Extra (teal-green fracture on white marble).

pattern.type: cloudy storm swirls with large cream patches

AMMAZZA.visual_description: A warm grey-brown marble interrupted by large cream-white cloudy patches that drift across the slab. The base leans warmer than Tempest and the cream patches are more dominant, but the two stones are near-identical stormy/cloudy marbles and are frequently paired. Softly neutral, warm, and subtly moody.
AMMAZZA.differentiator: Sister stone to Tempest — near-identical cloudy storm look. Slightly warmer grey-brown base with larger cream patches than Tempest. Both sit at the very light end of Browns. Lens should treat Tempest and Ammazza as a paired-confusion cluster.

color.accent: dark grey-black mineral shadows and warm rust flecks

pattern.type: large turquoise patches embedded in white crystalline matrix
pattern.vein_color: dark grey-black mineral shadows, rust flecks, fine white hairlines
pattern.vein_thickness: variable (thick cluster boundaries to fine filaments)
pattern.vein_density: medium — irregular turquoise patches dominate with darker accents in the matrix

AMOZONITA.visual_description: A turquoise-green semi-precious slab where the turquoise appears in irregular large patches embedded in a white-grey crystalline matrix with darker grey-black mineral shadows. Compared to Amazonite (which shows a uniform tessellated mosaic of turquoise cells), Amozonita reads patchier — the turquoise is concentrated in fewer but larger zones, with more visible white crystalline matrix between the green patches. Near-identical twin with Amazonite.
AMOZONITA.differentiator: Near-identical sister stone to Amazonite. Amozonita shows PATCHIER turquoise clusters with more visible white crystalline matrix between the green zones; Amazonite shows uniform tessellated mosaic cells with crisp dark edges. The density of white matrix is the differentiator — more white visible = Amozonita; more uniform green = Amazonite.

color.accent: white crystalline hairlines and black mineral pockets

pattern.type: plum field with darker wine shadow zones and fine white crystalline veins
pattern.vein_color: fine white, darker wine-purple, occasional black mineral
pattern.vein_density: medium — dense hairline network with soft cloud zones

ANCORA.visual_description: A dusty plum / mauve-purple marble with darker wine-red shadow zones and a dense network of fine white crystalline hairlines threading across the slab. Occasional black mineral pockets add depth. The plum reads warm-muted — not saturated-red, not pure-pink — a distinctive purple-pink middle ground.
ANCORA.differentiator: Dusty plum / mauve with fine white hairlines is distinctive — warmer and more purple than Red Lavante/Rosso Lavante (wine-reds), more saturated than Valle Rossa (pale pink), no dramatic crackle like Red Verona. The purple-plum middle ground is the ID.

pattern.type: cool grey field with darker grey crackle vein network
pattern.vein_color: darker grey, fine white, occasional warm rust-brown
pattern.vein_density: medium-dense — stony crackle pattern across a cool grey field

APHRODITE.visual_description: A cool grey-silver marble with a dense stony crackle vein network and occasional rust-brown edge accents. NOT pink or red despite name association — reads as a cool grey crackle marble. Similar in pattern and tone to Invictus and Caspian (both in Blues family) but without any blue cast — pure cool grey.
APHRODITE.differentiator: Cool grey crackle marble with rust edges — no blue cast (unlike Invictus/Caspian which lean blue-grey). Similar stony-crackle pattern. Not visually pink/red at all.

pattern.type: teal-green field with dense bright-white crystalline vein network and rust-brown accents
pattern.vein_color: bright white crystalline, rust-brown, warm gold filaments
pattern.vein_thickness: variable (dense branching veins and fine filaments)
pattern.vein_density: dense — full-coverage branching vein network with rust accent clusters

AQUA PATAGONIA EXTRA.visual_description: A vibrant teal-green quartzite with a dense branching network of bright white crystalline veins spreading across the slab, interrupted by warm rust-brown and gold filaments. Reads visually more as teal-green than pure blue — sits at the blue/green boundary and overlaps strongly with the Greens family. The white veining is dramatic and dense; the rust accents add warm contrast.
AQUA PATAGONIA EXTRA.differentiator: Vibrant TEAL-green base sets it apart — no other Blue reads this green. Dense bright-white vein network against a saturated teal field with rust accents. Lens should expect cross-family confusion with Greens (Verde Patagonia, Emerald).

color.accent: warm rust-orange and tan vein accents

pattern.type: horizontal wave bands with blue-grey and rust-orange accent veining
pattern.vein_color: blue-grey, bright white, warm rust-orange, tan
pattern.vein_thickness: medium horizontal wave bands with fine hairline accents
pattern.vein_density: dense — full-coverage horizontal wave pattern across the slab

AQUABELLA.visual_description: A cool grey-white marble with strongly horizontal wave banding — alternating lighter grey-white and blue-grey bands flow across the slab, interrupted by warm rust-orange and tan accent veins that add earthy contrast. The blue tone is stronger here than in Invisible Blue; the rust accents are a distinctive feature. Architectural and ornamental.
AQUABELLA.differentiator: Horizontal wave banding with distinctive WARM rust-orange accents is the hallmark — Invisible Blue sweeps diagonally (not horizontally) and lacks the rust, Azul Bahia has cloudy swirls (not horizontal waves), Invictus has stony crackle (not waves). The warm-cool contrast (rust + blue-grey) is unique in the family.

color.accent: occasional olive-green and darker brown shadows

pattern.type: sweeping painterly flows with soft multi-tone movement
pattern.vein_color: cream, pale gold, soft grey, olive-green traces
pattern.vein_density: medium — flowing painterly sweeps across the slab

ARTICO.visual_description: A soft warm-neutral quartzite in sweeping painterly flows of tan-beige, warm grey, cream, pale gold, and hints of olive-green. The tones are gentle and multi-layered, reading more as a cloudy warm-neutral landscape than a single dominant brown. Despite its cool-sounding name ('Artico'), the slab is decidedly warm.
ARTICO.differentiator: Soft multi-tone painterly flow with olive-green accents — lighter and more multi-chromatic than Fantasy Brown. Sits at the warm-neutral edge of the family, overlapping with Taupes and Beiges.

color.accent: distinctive red-brown and pink crackle veins

pattern.type: pale sage base with distinctive red-brown crackle vein network
pattern.vein_color: red-brown, pink, fine white hairlines, darker grey shadow
pattern.vein_density: medium — crackle pattern across the sage-green field

AVENTURINE.visual_description: A pale sage/seafoam green quartzite with a distinctive red-brown and pink crackle vein network spreading across the slab like fine lightning against a pale spring-green sky. The sage-green base is cool and muted; the red-pink crackle adds dramatic warm contrast. Visually unique in the family — no other Green has this red-crackle-on-sage combination.
AVENTURINE.differentiator: Pale sage-green base with RED-brown crackle vein network is unique in Greens — Emerald Harmony is pale sage but with subtle dark hairlines (no red), Verde Onyx is translucent with gold/brown accents (not red crackle), Verde Fusion is white-dominant. If the slab is pale green with pink-red crackle, it's Aventurine.

color.accent: bright white and cream crystalline veins

pattern.type: deep green field with lighter olive patches and bright white crystalline vein accents
pattern.vein_color: bright white, cream-yellow, occasional darker olive shadow
pattern.vein_density: medium — sweeping white vein accents against a predominantly-green base

AVOCADO.visual_description: A deep forest-green quartzite with lighter olive-green patches swirling across the slab and dramatic bright-white crystalline vein accents cutting through. The green is saturated and natural — evokes avocado flesh. Darker zones lean almost black-green, while lighter patches are mid-olive. The white veining is the visual hero against the uniformly-green base.
AVOCADO.differentiator: Deep forest-green with flowing white crystalline veins — darker and more saturated than Emerald Harmony (pale celadon), denser base than Verde Fusion (white-dominant). Near-twin with Avocatus; Avocado reads more uniformly deep-green with bright crisp white veins, while Avocatus reads more painterly-swirled with grey-green shadows (see Avocatus entry).

color.secondary: painterly swirled zones of lighter and darker green

pattern.type: painterly swirled olive-green field with grey-green shadow zones and white fracture veins
pattern.vein_color: bright white crystalline, darker olive-grey shadow
pattern.vein_thickness: variable (broad painterly flows and fine filaments)
pattern.vein_density: medium-dense — full-coverage swirling movement with white vein accents

AVOCATUS.visual_description: An olive-green quartzite with painterly swirling zones of lighter and darker green flowing across the slab like brushstrokes, interrupted by bright white crystalline fracture veins. The pattern is less uniform than Avocado (which has flatter green fields) — here the green tones mix and swirl more dramatically. Reads a touch warmer/khakier than Avocado.
AVOCATUS.differentiator: Near-twin with Avocado. Avocatus is more painterly-swirled with grey-green shadows breaking the green into flowing zones; Avocado reads flatter and more uniformly deep-green with crisper white veins. If the slab has brushstroke-like grey-green swirls, it's Avocatus; if it's flatter forest-green with bright white veins, it's Avocado.

pattern.type: white-cream base with diagonal grey-blue cloud sweeps and tan edges
pattern.vein_color: cool grey-blue, warm tan, occasional darker shadow
pattern.vein_density: medium — cloud-like diagonal sweeps against a predominantly white base

AZUL BAHIA.visual_description: A soft white-cream marble with dramatic diagonal cloud sweeps of cool grey-blue drifting across the slab like storm fronts on a pale sky, with warm tan-beige accents along some edges. The slab reads ~60% white/cream with striking blue-grey cloud zones — NOT a saturated blue stone. Trade-named 'Azul Bahia' but this Stonex variant leans white-with-blue-clouds rather than the famous deep royal-blue Brazilian Azul Bahia granite.
AZUL BAHIA.differentiator: White-dominant base with diagonal grey-blue CLOUD SWEEPS is the hallmark — Invisible Blue is smaller-scale diagonal streaks (not broad clouds), Aquabella is horizontal waves, Invictus is crackle-veined. Most white/least saturated-blue in the family.

color.accent: occasional soft blue-grey undertones in shadow zones

pattern.type: dense branching rust-brown hairline vein network on warm grey-white base
pattern.vein_color: rust-brown, warm tan, occasional soft blue-grey shadow

AZUL BRICHANI.visual_description: A warm grey-white marble with a dense branching network of rust-brown hairline veins spreading across the slab. The base has subtle grey-blue undertones in shadow zones, but the dominant read is warm-neutral — this is NOT a blue-appearing stone despite its trade name. The rust vein network is the visual hero. Looks closer to a Bulberry Beige or warm grey marble than any true blue.
AZUL BRICHANI.differentiator: Warm grey-white base with dense rust-brown hairline veining is the ID — does NOT visually read as blue. Azulado has dramatic rust diagonals (not networks), Caspian reads cooler with actual blue hints, Morinus Blue is pale pink-cream. Closest relative in collection visually is Bulberry Beige or a warm neutral marble.

pattern.type: banded / streaky

AZUL CALCITE.visual_description: A crystalline white calcite/quartzite dominated by soft, dreamy sky-blue wispy streaks flowing horizontally across the slab. The base is bright white but much of the surface reads as pale blue because the streaks are widespread. Reminiscent of frozen water or cloud movement.
AZUL CALCITE.differentiator: Most overtly blue stone in the Whites family — the blue is diffuse and wispy (like watercolor clouds) rather than the sharp, dark charcoal-blue fracture lines of Blu-ish White estremoz, and much more blue-dominant than Bianco Lazuli which reads essentially white. If someone describes a 'white stone that looks blue,' Azul Calcite is the answer.

color.accent: soft blue-grey undertones in shadow zones

pattern.type: dramatic rust-orange diagonal vein network on cool grey-white base
pattern.vein_color: bright rust-orange, warm tan, occasional soft blue-grey shadow
pattern.vein_thickness: medium diagonal veins with fine filament branches
pattern.vein_density: medium — distinctive diagonal vein network with warm colour against a cool base

AZULADO.visual_description: A cool grey-white marble scored with dramatic DIAGONAL rust-orange veins running across the slab, creating a strong warm-cool contrast against the pale blue-grey base. The rust colour is saturated and painterly, almost looking like copper lightning strikes through a cool sky. The blue is subtle and appears mostly in shadow zones of the base — the hero is really the rust veining, not the blue.
AZULADO.differentiator: DIAGONAL rust-orange veins on cool grey-white base — sharper and more dramatic than Azul Brichani (which is a fine network), cooler than Caspian (which has matching rust but more crackle), warmer-accented than Invictus (no rust). If the slab has dramatic diagonal rust on cool grey, it's Azulado.

pattern.type: uniform / near-solid

BASALTINO.visual_description: A solid mid-to-dark grey-black basalt (volcanic stone) with an almost uniform, near-solid surface. Only a very subtle diagonal grain is visible on close inspection. Reads as an architectural, understated near-black — the calmest, most pattern-free stone in the Blacks family.
BASALTINO.differentiator: The only true basalt (volcanic stone) in the Blacks family — distinctly different in texture and composition from the marble blacks. Uniform field with no veining, unlike every other Black which has some vein/pattern feature. Lighter and more neutral-grey than the pitch-black Black Marquina or Nero Saint Laurent.

surface.texture: porous (filled or unfilled depending on finish)

pattern.type: horizontally banded (travertine layered)

BEIGE TRAVERTINO.visual_description: A classic travertine with warm beige base and pronounced horizontal layered banding in cream and amber-tan tones. The signature look is the strong directional grain that gives every slab a sense of geological layering. Vein-cut shows the bands as horizontal lines; cross-cut shows them as pebbled clusters.
BEIGE TRAVERTINO.differentiator: The only true travertine in the Beiges family — defined by porous texture and strong horizontal layered banding. Other beiges are smooth marbles or limestones with cloud-veining; this one has signature 'tree-ring' style geological layers. Warmer and more golden than the limestone Mocca Cream and more directional than any of the cream marbles.

pattern.type: veined (fracture / lightning)

BIANCO ELIPTUS.visual_description: A crisp bright white marble dramatically crossed by sharp, branching rust-brown veining that looks like dark lightning strikes or cracked glass. The rust veins cluster in the upper section and fan outward in sharp angular lines, leaving the lower slab largely clean white. The contrast between the pristine white field and the intense copper fractures is the signature look.
BIANCO ELIPTUS.differentiator: Veins are rust-brown / copper rather than the grey of Statuario or Bianco Vogue, and are sharper and more linear (lightning-like) than Calacatta Makia Vakia's thick painterly gold+brown strokes. The white base is cleaner and brighter than Pirgon, and the rust veining is more concentrated/branching rather than the scattered amber streaks of Pirgon or Opus.

pattern.type: cloudy / subtle veined

BIANCO LASA.visual_description: A pure bright white marble with only faint cloudy grey mist and occasional hairline rust spots. The slab reads almost solid white from a distance — veining is present but extremely restrained. Clean, serene, and minimalist, with a luminous crystalline quality from the Italian Alps.
BIANCO LASA.differentiator: Cleaner and cooler-toned than Bianco Vogue (which has more pronounced horizontal mid-band movement) and slightly more visible grey misting than the near-uniform Thassos or Vietnam White. Not as pristine-white as Thassos but cleaner than Bianco Reale Cream. Lacks the warm gold hairlines of Bianco Lazuli.

pattern.type: subtly veined

BIANCO LAZULI.visual_description: A bright white marble with a very slight warm undertone and ultra-subtle warm gold / pale grey hairline veining. Reads almost solid white with just a soft cream glow. Gentle, understated, and clean.
BIANCO LAZULI.differentiator: Slightly warmer undertone than Bianco Lasa (which reads cooler) and carries faint gold hairlines rather than Bianco Lasa's pale grey. Much less dramatic than Statuario or Calacatta Caldiya. Less banded than Bianco Vogue which shows a horizontal stripe of movement.

pattern.type: fine branching vein network

BIANCO MORONUS.visual_description: A very pale cool grey marble (almost reading as white) with a delicate branching network of white hairline veins. Despite the 'Bianco' name, the base is a soft cool grey rather than true white. Calm, refined, with subtle vein structure.
BIANCO MORONUS.differentiator: Lightest of the Greys family — almost crosses into Whites territory. Distinguished by its delicate branching white vein network (rather than cloud movement). Cooler-toned than the Bulberry/Celina warm greys.

pattern.type: cloudy veined (Carrara-style)

BIANCO REALE CREAM.visual_description: A soft off-white marble showing Carrara-style cloudy blue-grey veining spread evenly across the slab. Despite the 'Cream' in the name, the undertone actually reads cool — the 'cream' refers to the softness rather than a warm hue. Uniform, calm, and classic.
BIANCO REALE CREAM.differentiator: Cloudy grey movement is more evenly distributed than Bianco Vogue (which has a pronounced horizontal mid-band). Grey veins are cooler and bluer than Statuario's darker greys. Not as pristine-white as Thassos or Vietnam White. Name is misleading — more cool than cream in reality.

pattern.type: cloudy / mottled
pattern.vein_density: moderate, soft mottling spread across surface

BIANCO SIENA.visual_description: A soft cream-beige marble with travertine-like cloudy mottling and faint amber and grey hairline veining. The pinkish-warm undertone gives it a gentle, sun-warmed look. Despite 'Bianco' (white) in the name, the dominant impression is warm beige rather than white.
BIANCO SIENA.differentiator: Compared to the more uniform Bulberry Beige, Bianco Siena shows more visible mottling and travertine-like cloud movement. Warmer pink undertone than Crema Marfil (which leans cool grey-beige) and lighter/creamier than its sister Crema Siena. The Italian-style cream beige despite the Turkish origin.

pattern.type: veined with horizontal banding
pattern.vein_density: moderate, with a distinctive horizontal stripe of denser veining through the middle

BIANCO VOGUE.visual_description: A bright white marble with fine grey hairline veins spread across a clean field, plus a signature horizontal band of denser veining running through the middle third of most slabs. The band gives directional movement while the rest reads calm and airy.
BIANCO VOGUE.differentiator: Horizontal mid-band stripe of denser veining is the signature — neither Bianco Lasa nor Bianco Reale Cream show this banded concentration. Less dramatic grey veining than Statuario, and not as purely uniform as Thassos or Vietnam White.

pattern.type: cloudy veined

BIANCO VOGUE 22400.visual_description: A specific block of the Bianco Vogue family (block 22400) showing a softly cloudy white surface with warm grey mist spread gently across the slab. Slightly warmer undertone and less pronounced banding than the main Bianco Vogue — more uniformly cloudy.
BIANCO VOGUE 22400.differentiator: A specific block variant of Bianco Vogue — softer and warmer-toned, lacking the bold horizontal mid-band veining seen in the main Bianco Vogue. Reads more uniformly cloudy than its parent block and has a mild warm tint that distinguishes it from cooler Bianco Lasa.

pattern.type: veined
pattern.vein_density: variable — from sparse single diagonals to dense crisscross networks

BLACK MARQUINA.visual_description: The classic Spanish black marble — a pitch black base crossed by crisp bright-white hairline veins. Across slabs the veining varies from a single minimalist sweep to dense crisscrossing networks. Pure, cool black-and-white contrast with no gold, brown, or warm undertones.
BLACK MARQUINA.differentiator: Pure cool black-and-white contrast with no gold veining — that's the clean differentiator from Nero Saint Laurent (which has prominent gold streaks). Darker and crisper than Grey Saint Laurent (which is brown-tinted). The simplest black-and-white story in the Blacks family; no warm elements.

pattern.type: dramatically veined
pattern.vein_color: charcoal blue-black with warm amber highlights
pattern.vein_density: moderate, concentrated as a dramatic central fracture

BLU-ISH WHITE ESTREMOZ.visual_description: A soft warm-white Portuguese Estremoz marble dramatically sliced by a nearly vertical fracture of dark charcoal-blue/black veining lined with copper-amber accents. The dramatic dark vein crashes down through the slab like lightning, with softer grey echoes elsewhere. Striking contrast between the calm white field and the explosive central vein.
BLU-ISH WHITE ESTREMOZ.differentiator: The dark vein is sharp, bold, and charcoal-BLUE/black — completely different from Azul Calcite's diffuse wispy sky-blue streaks. The amber linings around the dark vein add a warm counterpoint absent from Azul Calcite. Sister stone to Estremoz 22520 but with far more dramatic dark fracture instead of the delicate pink-tinted softness of 22520.

pattern.type: dramatically veined with central fracture
pattern.vein_density: moderate — concentrated as a dramatic central fracture

BLU-ISH WHITE ESTREMOZ (GREY-LEANING SLA.visual_description: The grey-dominant slabs of the Blu-ish White Estremoz Portuguese marble. While the white-leaning slabs (covered in the Whites family) emphasize the clean white field with the dramatic central blue-black fracture, the grey-leaning slabs feature a softer cool-grey base with the same dramatic fracture vein still as the hero. Same physical material — different slabs lean lighter or darker depending on the cut.
BLU-ISH WHITE ESTREMOZ (GREY-LEANING SLA.differentiator: Cross-family variant — same physical material as Blu-ish White Estremoz (in Whites) but describing the grey-dominant slabs. Defined by the same dramatic vertical blue-black fracture vein with amber linings — but on a cooler grey base instead of bright white. Sits between Greys and Blacks visually.

color.secondary: soft cream and white cloudy patches

pattern.type: soft icy-blue field with flowing cream patches and fine gold hairlines
pattern.vein_density: low-medium — gentle flowing movement on a pale icy-blue base

BLUE ONYX.visual_description: A rare translucent onyx with a pale icy powder-blue base, interrupted by soft cream cloudy patches and fine ochre-gold hairline veining. The blue is pastel and cool rather than saturated — more 'frozen pond' than 'royal blue'. Excellent for backlit applications where the icy colour glows. The quietest, softest blue in the family.
BLUE ONYX.differentiator: Only translucent onyx in the Blues family — all other blues are opaque marbles, quartzites, granites, or sodalites. Pale icy-blue base (pastel, not saturated) with gold hairlines. Backlit capable, unlike any other Blue in the collection.

color.accent: darker bronze shadows and white crystalline

pattern.type: vibrant teal-green field with diagonal rust-brown fracture veins
pattern.vein_density: medium — diagonal fracture pattern on a saturated teal base

BOTANIC.visual_description: A vibrant teal-green quartzite with strong diagonal rust-brown fracture veins spreading across the slab. The teal is saturated and tropical; the rust lines are directional, giving structure. Very similar to Aqua Patagonia Extra (Blues) and Verde Patagonia Extra (Greens) in the teal-green Patagonia family.
BOTANIC.differentiator: Vibrant teal-green with diagonal rust-brown fracture lines — sister to Verde/Aqua Patagonia Extra. Botanic reads slightly greener/less teal than Aqua Patagonia Extra. Lens should expect Patagonia-family cross-confusion.

pattern.type: quiet cream-beige field with subtle warm tan mineral clusters and faint veins

BOTTICINO.visual_description: The classic Italian Botticino marble — a pale cream-beige with subtle warm tan mineral hints and very faint darker grey hairlines. Quiet, architectural, heritage character. Among the most recognisable Italian beige marbles.
BOTTICINO.differentiator: Quieter than most Creme family stones — minimal pattern, soft warm-neutral field. Classical Italian heritage beige.

color.secondary: dense rust-brown and gold branching vein network
color.accent: darker grey mineral pockets and cream highlights

pattern.type: cream-beige field with dense rust-brown and gold branching vein network
pattern.vein_color: rust-brown, warm gold, darker grey, cream

BRECCIA AURA.visual_description: A warm cream-beige breccia marble with dense rust-brown and gold branching vein networks spreading across the slab like tree branches. The rust network is the visual hero against the cream base.
BRECCIA AURA.differentiator: Cream-beige with dense rust-brown branching network — more dense-veined than Botticino (quiet), warmer than Lavanto (grey-taupe base).

pattern.type: near-uniform with subtle hairline veining

BULBERRY BEIGE.visual_description: A warm, calm light-beige marble with a smooth uniform field and only the faintest white-cream hairline veining. Reads as nearly solid beige with a soft warm glow. Very versatile and understated.
BULBERRY BEIGE.differentiator: Among the Beiges, Bulberry Beige is one of the most uniform and pattern-free — fewer visible veins than Crema Marfil (which has clear gold hairlines) and warmer-toned than Bianco Siena (which leans creamy with travertine mottling). The closest in the family to a 'solid beige' field with only a hint of vein texture.

pattern.type: cloudy / mottled

BULBERRY GREY.visual_description: A warm, calm light-grey marble with soft taupe undertones and very subtle cream-white hairline veining. The cloud-like mottling is gentle rather than dramatic — reads as a refined warm grey, almost a 'beige-leaning grey.'
BULBERRY GREY.differentiator: Warmer-toned than the cool Carrara Grey or Ice Berg, and more uniformly mottled (less directional) than Grey Travertino. Among the calmest, most beige-leaning of the Greys family.

pattern.type: veined (varied)

CALACATTA CALDIYA.visual_description: A luminous bright white Calacatta marble with grey-and-gold veining that varies dramatically slab-to-slab — single bold diagonal strokes, dense storm-cloud clusters, delicate web networks, or horizontal grey banding all appear within the family. Grey dominates the veining, with gold playing a supporting role.
CALACATTA CALDIYA.differentiator: Grey-dominant veins with only hints of gold — the opposite balance of Calacatta Makia Vakia (gold-dominant with brown). Less pristine than Statuario which has cleaner, more defined grey veins against brighter white. More dramatic/varied slab-to-slab than Bianco Lasa or Vietnam White which are consistent across slabs.

pattern.type: boldly veined
pattern.vein_color: warm gold with dark brown cores
pattern.vein_thickness: thick bold strokes and surrounding hairlines

CALACATTA MAKIA VAKIA.visual_description: A dramatic bright white marble with bold warm-gold and dark brown veining forming an X-pattern across the slab. The main veins are thick and painterly, surrounded by finer gold hairlines. Much more gold-saturated than the other Calacattas — reads as a luxurious gold-on-white statement.
CALACATTA MAKIA VAKIA.differentiator: The gold is the hero here — not a supporting hairline like in Calacatta Caldiya (grey-dominant). Dark brown vein cores with gold outlines are unique to this stone. Much warmer overall than Statuario which is grey-on-white with cleaner, sharper veins.

color.secondary: dramatic warm gold and dark grey diagonal vein network

pattern.type: bright white field with dramatic diagonal gold and grey vein network
pattern.vein_color: warm gold, dark grey, fine rust
pattern.vein_thickness: thin to medium (diagonal veins and filaments)
pattern.vein_density: dense — dramatic full-coverage diagonal vein pattern

CALACATTA PICASSO.visual_description: A bright white marble with dramatic diagonal gold and dark grey vein network threading across the slab — classic high-end 'Calacatta' character with painterly gold veins (hence 'Picasso' in the name). Among the most dramatic Calacatta variants.
CALACATTA PICASSO.differentiator: Dramatic gold + grey diagonal network — more gold-saturated than standard Calacatta, more painterly than Statuario (crisp grey veins only).

pattern.type: dramatic horizontal wavy banding with charcoal, plum, sage-green, and cream zones

CAPOLAVORO.visual_description: A dramatic multi-color quartzite with dark charcoal and plum-purple swirls meeting pale sage-green and cream-white zones in horizontal wavy banding. The name 'Capolavoro' (masterpiece in Italian) suits the complex colour composition.
CAPOLAVORO.differentiator: Horizontal wavy banding with plum-purple + sage-green + charcoal — more purple-dominant than Forest Creek (mauve-grey), no teal like Pincelada.

color.secondary: dramatic white and grey swirly vein networks

pattern.type: dramatic white and grey swirls with gold filaments on dark grey-black base
pattern.vein_color: bright white, pale grey, warm gold-copper
pattern.vein_density: dense — full-coverage swirling vein network across a dark base

CARIBBEAN.visual_description: A dark grey-black marble with dramatic swirling white and pale-grey vein networks flowing across the slab, highlighted by warm gold-copper filaments. The slab reads predominantly DARK — not blue in the conventional sense. Trade-named 'Caribbean' but visually sits much closer to a dark grey / black marble than a blue stone. The swirling white veining is the visual hero.
CARIBBEAN.differentiator: Dark grey-black base with swirling white+gold veining — the DARKEST stone in the Blues family, with no actual blue pigment visible. Trade-named but not visually blue. Lens should expect strong cross-family confusion with Dark_Greys and Blacks.

pattern.type: cloudy with hairline veins
pattern.vein_density: moderate, evenly distributed web and cloud movement

CARRARA.visual_description: The quintessential Italian white marble. A cool-white base with evenly distributed grey cloudy veining and a fine network of hairline grey veins spread across the entire slab. No single bold vein dominates — the look is consistent, refined, and restrained. The benchmark classic white marble that most other 'Carrara-like' stones are compared against.
CARRARA.differentiator: The reference stone for the entire 'classic white marble' look. Compared to Statuario: Carrara has more evenly-distributed hairline veins and a slightly cooler grey undertone — Statuario is brighter white with more defined, bolder veins. Compared to Bianco Lasa: Carrara has more visible and denser veining. Compared to Bianco Vogue: Carrara has no horizontal banding concentration. More grey movement than Thassos or Vietnam White (which are near-solid whites).

pattern.type: dense crackle vein network (Carrara-style)

CARRARA GREY.visual_description: A grey-leaning Carrara variant — bright white-grey base with a dense crackle network of darker grey hairline veins spread across the slab. Reads as classic Carrara character with a cooler, greyer base than the standard cream-white Carrara.
CARRARA GREY.differentiator: The grey sister of the classic Carrara — same dense crackle vein character but on a noticeably cooler grey base. Much more vein-detailed than Bianco Moronus (which has only sparse white branching), and lighter than Grey Williams (which has true breccia structure).

color.secondary: horizontal wavy banding in pale grey and cream
color.accent: fine dark charcoal hairlines and warm amber edge

pattern.type: white base with soft horizontal wavy banding in pale grey and cream
pattern.vein_color: pale grey, cream, fine dark charcoal, occasional warm amber

CASABLANCA.visual_description: A white quartzite with soft horizontal wavy banding in pale grey and cream, like aerial view of layered mountain ranges. Fine dark charcoal hairlines add structure, with occasional warm amber edges. Elegant and architectural — the 'white house' in the name fits.
CASABLANCA.differentiator: Horizontal wavy banding in white-grey — more directional than Omni Bianco (crackle), softer than Alaska White (speckle).

pattern.type: dense blue-grey crackle / crazing vein network
pattern.vein_color: blue-grey, earthy rust-brown, fine white crystalline
pattern.vein_density: dense — full-coverage branching crackle network with subtle blue cast

CASPIAN.visual_description: A cool grey-white marble with a dense crackle/crazing vein network spread across the slab — most veins are soft blue-grey, but warm earthy rust-brown hairlines weave through for contrast. The blue is subtle, showing up in the vein colour and base cast rather than as a dominant field colour. Reads as an architectural crackle-marble with a cool blue undertone.
CASPIAN.differentiator: Dense crackle/crazing vein pattern with blue-grey + rust combo is the hallmark — Invictus also crackles but reads cooler/more uniformly grey without the rust, Invisible Blue has directional sweeps (not crackle), Aquabella has horizontal waves. The blue+rust vein combo is distinctive.

pattern.type: cloudy with soft veining

CELINA GREY.visual_description: A mid-tone warm grey marble with soft cloudy depth and occasional soft white hairline veining. Slightly warmer and slightly darker than Bulberry Grey, with more visible cloud movement giving the slab gentle drama.
CELINA GREY.differentiator: Slightly darker and more visibly cloudy than Bulberry Grey (which is more uniform). Warmer than the cool Ice Berg or Carrara Grey, and not as dramatic as Daisy Grey's bold white veining.

pattern.type: soft wispy flows with fine white hairline veins
pattern.vein_color: bright white crystalline hairlines and soft silvery-white flows
pattern.vein_density: medium — gentle wispy flows across a quiet cool-grey base

CHIANTI.visual_description: A very pale cool-grey marble with soft silvery-white wispy flows and fine bright-white hairline veins drifting gently across the slab. The base is quiet and crystalline, with subtle directional horizontal movement in some slabs and softer non-directional cloud-swirls in others. Reads as a near-white light grey — visually very close to Pantheon and the pale end of Estremoz, which is why it sits here rather than in Whites.
CHIANTI.differentiator: Very pale cool-grey with soft wispy white hairlines — reads near-white. Closest visual twin in the collection is Pantheon (Greys variant) — the two need careful side-by-side inspection to separate. Chianti tends to be slightly cooler and more uniform than Pantheon; Pantheon has more pronounced horizontal directional banding when banded variants are present. Less structured than Estremoz's cloud-streak pairing, softer than Dior Pearl's sparkle.

pattern.type: warm tan-brown field with dramatic horizontal cream-white band and rust-orange crystalline zone
pattern.vein_color: cream-white, rust-orange, black crystalline, fine grey
pattern.vein_thickness: broad horizontal band with fine crystalline accent

COLOSSAL.visual_description: A dramatic quartzite with warm tan-brown and grey zones split by a horizontal cream-white band running across the slab, accented by rust-orange crystalline edge zones. Like a cross-section of layered earth.
COLOSSAL.differentiator: Horizontal cream-white band against warm brown zones — distinctive layered composition.

color.accent: fine white crystalline and cream highlights

pattern.type: dark charcoal field with warm amber horizontal bands and fine white hairlines
pattern.vein_color: warm amber, cream, fine white, dark charcoal

CORTECCIA.visual_description: A dark grey-charcoal marble with warm amber horizontal bands and fine white crystalline hairlines threading across. The name 'Corteccia' (bark in Italian) fits — like tree bark with horizontal ridges. Darker and more structured than standard wood-grain marbles.
CORTECCIA.differentiator: Dark charcoal with warm amber horizontal bands — darker than Tobacco Brown, greyer than Indian Tobacco, more amber-warm than Ebony Travertino.

color.secondary: subtle grey and rust hairline veins

pattern.type: warm cream-yellow field with subtle grey and rust hairline veins

COSENTINO.visual_description: A warm cream-yellow marble with subtle grey and rust hairline veins and fine gold mineral streaks. Quiet warm-neutral character — reads as a pale giallo-cream marble.
COSENTINO.differentiator: Warm cream-yellow with subtle veining — quieter than Platinum Gold (saturated yellow), more yellow-tinted than Crema Marfil (classical cream).

pattern.type: dramatic gold-veined explosion
pattern.vein_density: dense — explosive gold bursts and branching gold rivers across the black base

COSMIC GOLD.visual_description: A spectacular Indian quartzite with a deep black base lit up by dramatic clusters of gold and copper veining that explode across the slab like cosmic starbursts or molten gold pouring through volcanic rock. The gold is rich, saturated, and painterly — the hero of the stone. Among the most dramatic 'black and gold' looks available.
COSMIC GOLD.differentiator: Most dramatic gold-on-black in the family — gold clusters are thick and painterly, not thin streaks like Nero Saint Laurent's vertical gold hairlines. Much more gold-saturated than any other Black. Quartzite (not marble), giving it a crystalline gleam. If 'black with explosive gold' is the brief, this is the stone.

color.accent: occasional rose-grey shadows and fine white crystalline veins

pattern.type: cream-white onyx field with soft warm tan sweeping waves and rose-grey shadows
pattern.vein_color: warm tan, rose-grey, fine white crystalline
pattern.vein_density: medium — directional wave pattern on a pale cream base

CREAM WAVE ONYX.visual_description: A translucent cream-white onyx with soft warm tan sweeping waves drifting diagonally across the slab and occasional rose-grey shadow zones. Fine white crystalline vein filaments add sparkle. A quiet, elegant, warm onyx — backlit-capable.
CREAM WAVE ONYX.differentiator: Cream-white onyx with warm tan sweeping WAVES — distinct from Icicle Onyx (pure icy-white) and Peach Onyx (peachier). Directional wave pattern is the ID. Backlit-capable translucent onyx.

color.shade: warm with cool grout-like vein contrast

pattern.type: breccia / mosaic
pattern.vein_density: dense — cream pebbles separated by continuous vein network covering most of the slab

CREMA ELYSEE.visual_description: A dramatic breccia-style beige marble where the slab looks like a mosaic of cream-beige pebbles cemented together by an olive-grey/rust vein network filling the gaps between them. Each pebble is a soft warm cream; the network gives the slab strong visual texture. Looks ancient and architectural — like a polished Roman wall.
CREMA ELYSEE.differentiator: The only true breccia-pattern stone in the Beiges — instantly distinguishable by its mosaic of cream pebbles and olive-grey vein network. All other Beiges are veined or cloudy/uniform. If a slab looks like 'beige stones glued together with grout lines,' it's Crema Elysee.

color.accent: soft amber and grey hairline veins

pattern.type: veined and cloudy
pattern.vein_density: moderate, scattered evenly with occasional shadow zones

CREMA MARFIL.visual_description: A classic light beige marble with a slightly cooler grey-cream undertone (not as warm as cream-toned beiges) and visible soft amber-and-grey hairline veining scattered across the slab. Some slabs show smoky cloudy zones layered with the veins. The international benchmark for 'beige marble' — restrained, classic, and timeless.
CREMA MARFIL.differentiator: Slightly cooler beige than Bianco/Crema Siena (which lean warm pink-cream) and more visibly veined than Bulberry Beige (which is near-uniform). The reference 'classic beige marble' worldwide. Lacks the dramatic breccia pattern of Crema Elysee and the pinker tone of Crema Uno or Crema Purrisima.

pattern.type: fine crackle / web
pattern.vein_density: moderate — fine crackling network across the surface

CREMA PURRISIMA.visual_description: A pale peach-cream marble with a delicate crackling network of fine amber-rust hairline veins spread evenly across the slab like cracked porcelain or fine craquelure. Soft pink-warm base, very feminine and delicate.
CREMA PURRISIMA.differentiator: Pinker, warmer base than Crema Marfil (which is more neutral) and finer crackling than Spider Beige. The hairline crackle network is its signature — like delicate craquelure on porcelain. Renamed officially to 'Persian Marfil' per Stonex rebranding sheet.

pattern.type: uniform with subtle dappling

CREMA SIENA.visual_description: A warm creamy beige marble with very subtle dappled mottling — almost reads as a single soft cream tone with delicate texture. Lighter and creamier than Bianco Siena, with no visible vein lines. Quiet, warm, classic.
CREMA SIENA.differentiator: Lighter and creamier than its sibling Bianco Siena (which has more amber/grey mottling) and more uniform than Crema Marfil (which carries visible gold hairlines). One of the most pure 'cream' Beiges — almost no veining, just gentle warmth.

pattern.type: subtly veined
pattern.vein_density: sparse — scattered fine white branching veins

CREMA UNO.visual_description: A pale peach-pink cream marble with delicate white hairline veining scattered across a uniform field. Slightly pinker than most beiges, with crisp white veins that contrast against the warm base. Quiet and refined.
CREMA UNO.differentiator: White veins are the distinguishing feature — most other Beiges have amber/rust hairlines instead. Pinker base than Crema Marfil and more linear veining than the crackle pattern of Crema Purrisima. Less mottled than Bianco Siena.

pattern.type: veined / translucent

CRYSTAL YELLOW ONYX.visual_description: A translucent white-to-cream onyx with crystalline luminosity and soft amber hairline veining running diagonally. Despite 'Yellow' in the name, the stone reads predominantly pale cream-white with only whispers of warm yellow. Best viewed backlit to reveal the crystal glow.
CRYSTAL YELLOW ONYX.differentiator: Lighter and cooler-toned than most 'yellow onyx' varieties — reads closer to white than gold. Lacks the rust-orange fractures of White Onyx and the dramatic amber streaks of Taj Mahal. Most pastel/delicate of the onyxes in the collection.

pattern.type: cream-gold base with bold dark charcoal diagonal veining bands
pattern.vein_color: dark charcoal, bronze-gold, cream, fine white
pattern.vein_thickness: thick diagonal bands with fine filaments

CYGNUS.visual_description: A cream-gold and warm tan quartzite with bold dark charcoal diagonal bands sweeping across the slab, accented by bronze-gold filaments. Dramatic warm-dark contrast with strong directional movement.
CYGNUS.differentiator: Cream-gold base with bold dark charcoal diagonal bands — more gold-warm than Parquet (orange-black), more banded than Fuego (zone-split).

pattern.type: dramatic bold white branching veining

DAISY GREY.visual_description: A mid-dark grey marble dramatically streaked with thick bright-white branching veins that crisscross the slab like roots or lightning. Very high contrast — the white veining pops against the darker grey base. One of the most graphic, statement-making Greys.
DAISY GREY.differentiator: Boldest white-on-grey contrast in the family — the white veins are thick painterly strokes, not hairlines. Much more dramatic than Bulberry Grey or Celina Grey (which are calm). Less dark than Hermes Grey (which is near-black) and not breccia-like (unlike Grey Williams).

pattern.type: fine white and gold hairline veining on dark brown base

DARK EMPERADOR.visual_description: The classic dark chocolate-brown Spanish marble with a network of fine white and warm-gold hairline veins scattered diagonally across the slab. The brown base is consistently rich and saturated, and the white veining is crisp and linear (not a cream lattice). A benchmark stone — most 'brown marble with white veins' references point here.
DARK EMPERADOR.differentiator: Fine crisp white hairlines on uniform chocolate base — less dense than Tropical Storm's lattice, less crackled than French Brown's pebble-net. The classic benchmark for 'brown marble with thin white veins.'

color.accent: fine rust and darker grey hairlines

pattern.type: pale cream-beige field with subtle horizontal mineral grain
pattern.vein_color: warm tan, fine rust, darker grey

DIANO.visual_description: Classic Italian Diano marble — a pale cream-beige with subtle warm tan horizontal grain and fine rust and darker grey hairlines. Heritage Italian beige character, softer and more horizontal than Botticino.
DIANO.differentiator: Classic warm cream-beige with subtle horizontal grain — sister to Botticino but with more directional movement.

pattern.type: near-solid / minimal

DIOR PEARL.visual_description: An extremely uniform, pearl-white marble with almost no visible veining or movement. Reads as a single, softly luminous off-white plane. Minimalist, understated, serene.
DIOR PEARL.differentiator: Warmer pearl tone than Thassos (which is pure cool white) and Vietnam White (which is cleaner and more sterile). Reads more like soft cream-pearl than snow-white. No veining at all — the quietest stone in the family alongside Thassos and Vietnam White.

color.secondary: dense black crystalline clusters and diagonal vein network

pattern.type: bright white field with dense black crystalline cluster patterns and diagonal vein network

DOLCHEVITA BRAZILIAN.visual_description: A bright white-silver Brazilian granite/quartzite with dense dark-black crystalline clusters and diagonal vein network spreading across the slab. High-contrast 'sweet life' composition — dramatic salt-and-pepper with a painterly edge.
DOLCHEVITA BRAZILIAN.differentiator: Dense black clusters with diagonal structure — more painterly than Genesis (speckled), less horizontal than Patagonia.

pattern.type: painterly / topographic

DOVER WHITE.visual_description: A bright white marble punctuated by dramatic topographic pools of dark charcoal-black and warm amber that look like cave networks, islands, or abstract landscapes. The dark zones cluster in organic shapes while the rest of the slab stays pristine white. Painterly and artistic — more like a landscape painting than typical marble veining.
DOVER WHITE.differentiator: Landscape/topographic pooling of dark veining — completely different from Nebula's flowing swirled marbling. Darker and more dramatic than any Calacatta's grey veins. More painterly and organic than the sharp lightning fractures of Bianco Eliptus.

color.accent: distinctive pink-rose hairline rims and darker rust lines

pattern.type: pale yellow-gold horizontal band flanked by cream-white zones and pink-rose hairline rims
pattern.vein_density: medium — distinct horizontal band layers with rose rim accents

DRAGON ONYX.visual_description: A translucent onyx with a distinctive pale yellow-gold horizontal band through the middle, flanked by cream-white zones above and below, and edged by pink-rose hairline rims. The yellow-gold gives it a soft glow when backlit; the pink rose rims are the signature. Quiet pastel pastel band composition.
DRAGON ONYX.differentiator: Three-zone horizontal composition (cream / yellow-gold / cream with rose rims) is unique — Pink Onyx has orange band (not yellow), Peach Onyx is faint peach without banding, Cream Wave Onyx has tan sweeping waves. If the slab has a yellow-gold central band with pink rims, it's Dragon Onyx.

surface.texture: porous travertine with strong layered banding

pattern.type: horizontally banded (travertine layers)
pattern.vein_color: taupe, silver, darker grey-brown, occasional rust

EBONY TRAVERTINO.visual_description: A dark grey-brown travertine with strong horizontal layered banding in taupe, silver, and darker tones with occasional rust streaks. Despite the 'Ebony' (black) name, the slab reads as a deep earth-tone dark rather than true black — it is the darkest of the travertines but not a pitch black.
EBONY TRAVERTINO.differentiator: The only true travertine in the Blacks family — defined by its porous texture and horizontal layered banding, unlike the smooth veined marble blacks. Lighter than 'true blacks' (Black Marquina, Nero Saint Laurent) — sits at the dark end of the Browns or the warm end of the Blacks. Sister to lighter travertines like Grey Travertino and Silver Travertino (both in Greys).

color.accent: occasional subtle teal-green hints in shadow zones

pattern.type: silvery-white crystalline field with rust-brown sweeping streaks
pattern.vein_color: rust-brown, fine white, occasional subtle teal shadow
pattern.vein_thickness: variable (broad sweeping streaks and fine filaments)
pattern.vein_density: medium — directional movement on a silvery-white base

EMERALD CRYSTALLO.visual_description: A silvery-white crystalline quartzite with sweeping rust-brown streaks flowing across the slab and occasional subtle teal-green hints in shadow zones. Despite the 'Emerald' name, visually this reads as a silvery-white stone with warm rust accents rather than a green stone. The crystalline body gives it brilliance.
EMERALD CRYSTALLO.differentiator: Silvery-white crystalline with rust-brown sweeping streaks — NOT a green stone despite 'Emerald' name. The green only appears subtly in shadow zones.

color.secondary: dramatic copper-orange and amber painterly zones

pattern.type: pale teal base with dramatic copper-orange painterly flame zones and dark crackle
pattern.vein_color: copper-orange, warm amber, dark charcoal-grey crackle, fine rust
pattern.vein_thickness: variable (broad painterly amber zones and fine crackle filaments)
pattern.vein_density: medium-dense — dramatic painterly transitions across the slab

EMERALD FLAME.visual_description: A dramatic quartzite where a pale teal-green base meets sweeping copper-orange and warm amber zones — like green flames meeting fiery copper. Fine dark network crackle cuts across the whole slab for added texture. The strong warm-cool contrast makes it one of the most visually striking stones in the family. No two slabs are alike — the flame/amber zones move dramatically.
EMERALD FLAME.differentiator: Dramatic WARM COPPER flame zones on teal-green base is the signature — no other Green has this level of warm painterly contrast. Verde Patagonia has jagged fractures (not flame zones), Verde Fusion has lime-green swirls on white (not teal + copper), Aventurine has red crackle but stays pale overall. If the slab shows teal-and-copper painterly fire, it's Emerald Flame.

pattern.type: quiet sage base with fine dark hairline crackle
pattern.vein_color: dark charcoal-grey, occasional warm amber filaments
pattern.vein_density: low-medium — subtle crackle pattern across a quiet sage field

EMERALD HARMONY.visual_description: A clean soft sage / celadon green quartzite with a quiet, gentle pattern — the green base is uniform and muted, interrupted only by fine dark hairline crackle veins. No dramatic contrast, no swirls, no painterly movement — the harmony in the name reflects the stone's restraint. The quietest, most architectural green in the family.
EMERALD HARMONY.differentiator: Quiet sage-green with only fine dark hairlines — the least-patterned Green in the family. Aventurine has dramatic red crackle (Harmony has none), Verde Onyx is translucent with warm accents (Harmony is opaque quartzite), Verde Fusion is white-dominant with vibrant lime swirls. If the slab is uniformly-soft sage with minimal movement, it's Emerald Harmony.

color.accent: dark mineral pockets and occasional warm amber hints

pattern.type: cool grey-white base with soft sweeping grey crackle veins and dark mineral pockets
pattern.vein_color: darker grey, fine white, amber hint, dark mineral
pattern.vein_density: medium — soft sweeping pattern with occasional dark pocket accents

ENIGMA.visual_description: A cool grey-white marble with soft sweeping grey crackle veins and occasional dark mineral pockets. Quiet and architectural — sits in the Light_Greys family despite exotic trade-naming. Similar in character to Invictus or Caspian (Blues) but without any blue cast.
ENIGMA.differentiator: Cool grey-white with soft sweeping grey veins — less dramatic than Invictus, quieter than Pantheon Grey.

pattern.type: subtly veined with fracture accents

ESTREMOZ 22520.visual_description: A delicate warm-white Portuguese Estremoz marble with a faint pink-peach undertone and occasional small clusters of amber rust and charcoal hairline veining. The dominant impression is a gentle warmth — the stone almost blushes. Much softer and pinker than its sister 'Blu-ish White Estremoz'.
ESTREMOZ 22520.differentiator: Shares the Portuguese Estremoz origin with Blu-ish White Estremoz but is the quiet, warm-pink cousin — no dramatic blue-black fracture, just delicate pink glow with occasional amber hits. The only pink-tinted stone in the Whites family.

pattern.type: soft crackle with cream and gold fine veining
pattern.vein_density: medium — fine crackling against a mid-brown base

FANTASY BROWN.visual_description: A soft mid-brown Indian quartzite with a subtle cream-and-gold crackle pattern drifting across the slab. Much lighter and softer than Dark Emperador or Tropical Storm — the brown here is warm and muted rather than chocolate-rich. The gold-tan filaments give it a gentle shimmer in good light. Sits between Browns and Beiges.
FANTASY BROWN.differentiator: Soft muted mid-brown quartzite (not dark chocolate marble). Far lighter than Dark Emperador or Tropical Storm. Fine gold-cream crackle instead of dominant veining. Pairs as a 'light brown crystalline' entry in the family.

pattern.type: cloudy with soft directional grain

FERRAGAMOE BEIGE.visual_description: A warm cream-beige limestone with travertine-like cloudy texture and gentle horizontal grain. Reads as a sun-warmed natural beige — softer and more textural than smooth marble beiges. The slab labeling typically reads 'FERRAGAMA_BEIGE' (block markings).
FERRAGAMOE BEIGE.differentiator: Limestone texture (more porous and matte than marble) sets it apart from marble beiges like Crema Marfil. Warmer and softer-grained than Mocca Cream (which is more uniformly pale) and less directionally banded than Beige Travertino. Mid-toned warm beige limestone.

color.accent: faint white hairlines and soft cloudy zones

pattern.type: soft cloudy with horizontal grain hint

FLORTINE BEIGE.visual_description: A smooth warm light-beige marble with travertine-like horizontal grain and faint white hairline veining. The slab reads as gently warm cream-beige with soft directional movement — calm and easy to use in volume.
FLORTINE BEIGE.differentiator: More directional travertine-style grain than Bulberry Beige (which is non-directional) and less mottled than Bianco Siena. A 'middle-of-the-road' warm beige — versatile, restrained, with subtle but visible texture.

pattern.type: near-uniform with directional grain

FONTANA.visual_description: A warm peach-beige limestone with soft horizontal grain and an almost uniform field. Reads as warmly pink-tinted compared to other beiges — the warmth is its signature. Calm and inviting, like sun-baked Mediterranean stone.
FONTANA.differentiator: Limestone (not marble), with a distinctly warmer pink-peach tone than the cooler Mocca Cream. More uniform than Crema Uno (which has visible white hairline veins) and warmer-toned than Beige Travertino (which has more pronounced banding). The warmest pink-tinted stone in the Beiges family.

color.accent: darker charcoal shadow zones and warm gold filaments

pattern.type: dramatic horizontal wavy banding with grey-mauve, cream-peach, and charcoal zones

FOREST CREEK.visual_description: A painterly quartzite with dramatic horizontal wavy banding blending grey-mauve, cream-peach, and charcoal shadow zones — like layers of a creek bed in soft evening light. Multi-tonal warm-cool mix.
FOREST CREEK.differentiator: Horizontal wavy banding with grey-mauve + cream-peach + charcoal — softer and more mauve-dominant than Pincelada (multi-color bolder), no teal like Pincelada.

color.accent: black shadow pockets and fine silver hairlines

pattern.type: dark green-charcoal field with bold diagonal white crystalline vein network
pattern.vein_color: bright white crystalline, fine silver, black shadow
pattern.vein_density: dense — diagonal vein pattern across a dark green-black base

FORRESTA RUGGED.visual_description: A dark green-charcoal marble with dramatic diagonal bright-white crystalline vein network spreading across the slab and black shadow pockets. Darker and more angular than Verde Vermont — the 'rugged' in the name fits.
FORRESTA RUGGED.differentiator: Darker than Verde Vermont with bolder diagonal white crystalline veins — more dramatic and angular. If the slab is dark-green-black with diagonal white crystals, it's Forresta Rugged.

pattern.type: dense pebble-like white crackle across a dark brown base
pattern.vein_density: very dense — pebble/web crackle covering much of the slab

FRENCH BROWN (ORIENTAL COCOA).visual_description: A dark chocolate brown marble overlaid with a dense pebble-like network of bright white crackle veining that covers much of the slab — visually reminiscent of dark chocolate with a web of cream mineral cracks. Denser and brighter-white than Dark Emperador's hairlines, and tighter-webbed than Tropical Storm's lattice.
FRENCH BROWN (ORIENTAL COCOA).differentiator: Dense pebble/web crackle in bright white (not cream) on a dark brown base. More network-web than Dark Emperador's scattered hairlines and whiter/tighter than Tropical Storm's cream lattice. Trade-renamed 'Oriental Cocoa' in some catalogues.

color.accent: cool white and grey marble sections, gold filaments

pattern.type: painterly flowing zones — fiery copper-orange meeting cool white marble
pattern.vein_color: rich copper-orange, dark chocolate, gold, cool white, pale grey
pattern.vein_thickness: variable (broad painterly zones and fine gold filaments)
pattern.vein_density: medium — dramatic zone-based transitions across the slab

FUEGO.visual_description: A dramatic quartzite where a fiery copper-orange to dark chocolate zone sweeps across one half of the slab like a wildfire, while the other half is a cool white marble with grey and gold filament veining — 'fuego' (fire) meeting ice. The zone boundary is painterly and gradient, not a hard edge. Among the most dramatic warm stones available; no two slabs are alike.
FUEGO.differentiator: Dramatic two-zone composition (fiery orange meeting cool white) is unique in Oranges — no other Orange has this split painterly character. Tramonto is fully orange-red across the slab; Fuego splits between orange and white. The gradient fire-to-ice transition is the hallmark.

pattern.type: exotic multicolor swirled
pattern.vein_color: black, dark grey, cream, occasional rust

FUSION BLACK.visual_description: A dramatic French quartzite with flowing multicolor swirls combining black, dark grey, cream, and occasional rust tones in a painterly pattern. Despite the 'Black' in the name, the slab reads as a MULTICOLOR exotic rather than a true black — the black is one of several tones working together rather than the dominant base. Better described as 'fusion of dark and light' than 'black.'
FUSION BLACK.differentiator: The least 'black' stone in the Blacks family — actually a multicolor exotic with only black as one of several tones. If the application calls for a true black field, Fusion Black is the wrong pick; if the application calls for dramatic multicolor with black accents, it's perfect.

color.secondary: scattered dark black speckles and clusters
color.accent: occasional warm amber and grey mineral clusters

pattern.type: bright white-silver field with scattered dark black speckles and crystalline clusters
pattern.vein_color: dark black speckle, warm amber, grey

GENESIS.visual_description: A bright white-silver crystalline granite with scattered dark black speckles and clusters — classic 'salt and pepper' granite. Reads predominantly white with heavy dark speckling.
GENESIS.differentiator: Bright white with heavy dark speckle — similar to Alaska White but more saturated in black speckles, denser pattern than Panda White (which is cloudy, not speckled).

pattern.type: quiet warm silvery-grey field with scattered micro-speckles
pattern.vein_color: subtle tan and darker grey specks

GRANELLO.visual_description: A quiet warm silvery-grey limestone with very subtle tan undertones and scattered micro-speckles. Minimal pattern — a background stone with matte sedimentary character. The name 'Granello' (little grain in Italian) suits its speckle texture.
GRANELLO.differentiator: Quiet warm-grey limestone with micro-speckle texture — sister to Lusso in the quiet warm-grey category.

color.accent: olive-green patches and dark charcoal / black mineral shadows

pattern.type: flowing painterly swirls with bright white crystalline splashes on a dark grey-green base
pattern.vein_color: bright white crystalline, olive-green, dark charcoal / black shadow
pattern.vein_thickness: variable (broad flowing splashes and fine filaments)
pattern.vein_density: medium-dense — full-coverage swirling movement with bold white accents

GREEN JADEZCALA.visual_description: A dark grey-green granite with bright white crystalline flowing splashes and olive-green patches swirling across the slab. The dark base is the dominant read (~70% of the slab), interrupted by dramatic bold-white crystalline zones and scattered darker charcoal mineral shadows. The flowing / swirled pattern direction is the hallmark — like a dark stormy sea with bright foam caps. Trade-named 'Green Jadezcala' but visually sits on the Dark_Greys / Greens border, leaning darker.
GREEN JADEZCALA.differentiator: Dark grey-green granite with bright white flowing splashes — closer in color to the Dark_Greys / Greens border than to pure Blacks. Distinguished from Verde Vermont (which is more uniformly forest-green with denser crackle veining) by its painterly swirled movement and grey-dominant shadows. Distinguished from Avocado/Avocatus by being GREYER / less saturated-green.

color.accent: occasional dark olive-green undertone in shadow zones

pattern.type: dense bright white crackle vein network on a black base
pattern.vein_color: bright white (dense branching network), occasional dark olive hint
pattern.vein_density: very dense — full-coverage crackle network across a black field

GREEN LAVANTE.visual_description: A deep-black marble overlaid with a dense network of bright-white crackle veins that spread across the slab like fractured porcelain. Trade-named 'Green Lavante' suggesting a green stone, but visually this reads as a classic BLACK marble with white crackle — the green undertone is only barely present in shadow zones. Closest visual twin is Grigio Fusion (Calacatta Black) in the Blacks family.
GREEN LAVANTE.differentiator: Near-identical visual look to Grigio Fusion (Calacatta Black) — both are black marble with dense white crackle. Green Lavante tends to show faint olive-green undertones in shadow zones (Grigio Fusion is pure cool-black), which is the only reliable differentiator. Trade-named 'Green' but visually sits firmly in Blacks.

pattern.type: dense crackle / watercolor cloud
pattern.vein_density: dense crackle web with cloud movement

GREY BARDILO.visual_description: A cool blue-grey marble with dense white crackle veining and watercolor cloud movement flowing diagonally. The blue-grey base reads cool and oceanic, the white veining gives a frosted glass / iceberg appearance. Italian Bardiglio character with extra cool tone.
GREY BARDILO.differentiator: Cooler and more blue-tinted than the other Greys — the only one that genuinely feels icy/oceanic. Denser crackle veining than Ice Berg (which has more horizontal grain), and bolder than Carrara Grey's classic crackle.

pattern.type: near-uniform with subtle cloud
pattern.vein_color: very faint cream and darker grey

GREY FLURRY.visual_description: A mid-tone grey marble that reads almost as a solid uniform field with only the subtlest cloud movement and barely-visible hairline cracks. One of the calmest, most pattern-free greys — like a soft fog field. Excellent for backgrounds.
GREY FLURRY.differentiator: The most uniform / pattern-free of the Greys family — no defined veins or breccia structure, just calm flat grey. Cooler-neutral than Bulberry/Celina (warm), darker than Bianco Moronus (very pale), and lighter/cleaner than Hermes Grey.

pattern.type: branching white fracture veining
pattern.vein_color: bright white with occasional faint gold

GREY SAINT LAURENT.visual_description: A very dark brown-black marble of the Saint Laurent family crossed by sharp, branching white veins that look like lightning strikes across the dark base. Lighter and browner than Nero Saint Laurent and with prominent white (rather than gold) veining. Appears almost black under dim light; reveals warm brown undertones in direct light.
GREY SAINT LAURENT.differentiator: The brown-black sibling of Nero Saint Laurent — same Saint Laurent family character but with WHITE (not gold) veining and a warmer brown undertone. More dramatic branching than Nero's sparse vertical streaks. Darker and warmer than the cool Black Marquina. Note: this stone also appears in the Greys family as it sits at the border; the Blacks JSON describes it as it reads in darker / lower-light conditions.

color.secondary: dramatic diagonal gold and rust vein streaks
color.accent: dark charcoal shadow pockets with white crystalline

pattern.type: warm grey-taupe field with dramatic diagonal gold and rust streaks and dark crystalline pockets
pattern.vein_color: warm gold, rust, dark charcoal, white crystalline

GREY SARAN COLINE.visual_description: A warm grey-taupe marble with dramatic diagonal gold and rust vein streaks and dark charcoal shadow pockets punctuated by white crystalline clusters. Multi-tonal warm-cool exotic. User previously excluded from Greys family for being too complex/warm.
GREY SARAN COLINE.differentiator: Warm grey-taupe with dramatic gold + rust diagonal streaks and crystalline pockets — distinct multi-color complexity.

pattern.type: horizontally banded (travertine layers)

GREY TRAVERTINO.visual_description: A warm dark-grey travertine with strong horizontal layered banding in tan, cream, and rust-amber tones. The signature travertine 'tree-ring' layering is the hero. Despite the 'Grey' name, the dominant impression is warm dark earth-tones rather than cool grey.
GREY TRAVERTINO.differentiator: The only true travertine in the Greys family with strong horizontal layered banding — completely different from the smooth marble greys. Warmer and darker than Silver Travertino which leans pale beige.

color.accent: gold and rust hairlines between pieces

pattern.type: breccia / mosaic
pattern.vein_density: dense — fragmented stone pieces with continuous vein matrix

GREY WILLIAMS.visual_description: A dramatic mid-dark grey breccia marble — the slab looks like fragmented grey stone pieces of varying sizes cemented together by a network of gold and cream connective veining. Each 'pebble' is a different shade of grey, giving the slab strong textural depth. Architectural, ancient feel.
GREY WILLIAMS.differentiator: The signature grey breccia/mosaic of the family — the only Grey with true 'fragmented stones cemented by gold veins' character. Different from Oreo Grey which has a brighter cream base with grey pebbles. Far more textural than the smooth Bulberry/Celina/Grey Flurry. User-confirmed all three Williams variants (Williama, Williams, Williams Italy) are the same stone.

pattern.type: dramatic cloudy storm
pattern.vein_color: darker grey clouds and white patches

GRIGIO FIASCO.visual_description: A cool mid-grey marble with dramatic cloudy storm-like movement across the slab — darker grey patches sweep into lighter zones with occasional white inclusions. Reads like a stormy sky frozen in stone. 'Grigio' is Italian for grey.
GRIGIO FIASCO.differentiator: Most dramatic cloudy movement of the cool greys — like a stormy sky vs the calm fog of Grey Flurry. Cooler than Grigio Trambisera (which has warm gold accents), and more cloud-driven than the crackle-veined Grey Bardilo or Carrara Grey.

pattern.type: dense crackle / fracture veining
pattern.vein_density: dense — full-coverage crackle network across the slab

GRIGIO FUSION (CALACATTA BLACK).visual_description: A dramatic pitch-black marble overlaid with a dense network of bright white crackle veining spreading across the slab like cracked porcelain. Much more dense and web-like than Black Marquina's crisp individual veins — here the white network dominates equally with the black field. Renamed officially to 'Calacatta Black' per Stonex rebranding sheet.
GRIGIO FUSION (CALACATTA BLACK).differentiator: Dense crackle/web vein pattern is the key differentiator from Black Marquina (which has sparse crisp veins). More network-heavy than any other Black in the family — the white occupies nearly as much visual space as the black. Official trade rename notes that this is effectively a 'Calacatta pattern on black base.'

pattern.type: soft breccia / cluster with hairline veining

GRIGIO TRAMBISERA.visual_description: A warm light grey Italian marble with soft breccia-like clusters of pale and amber tones, accented by gold hairline veining. The warm gold accents distinguish it from cooler greys — feels Italian sun-warmed even though it's a grey.
GRIGIO TRAMBISERA.differentiator: The warmest grey of the family with visible amber-gold accents — distinguishes it from the cool stormy Grigio Fiasco (its Italian neighbor). Less multicolor than Grey Saran Coline.

color.secondary: dramatic white crystalline and warm gold vein network

pattern.type: cool grey-white field with dramatic white crystalline and warm gold vein network
pattern.vein_color: bright white crystalline, warm gold, darker grey

GRIS MORRO.visual_description: A cool grey-white marble with dramatic bright-white crystalline and warm gold vein network spreading across the slab. The name 'Gris' (grey in Spanish) fits; the gold accents elevate it.
GRIS MORRO.differentiator: Cool grey-white with bold white crystalline + warm gold network — the gold elevates it above pure greys.

pattern.type: dense crackle vein network
pattern.vein_density: dense crackle network across most of slab

HERMES GREY.visual_description: A very dark charcoal-near-black marble overlaid with a dense network of bright white crackle veining that branches across the surface like cracked porcelain. The contrast is extreme — dark base, bright cracks. One of the darkest stones in the Greys family — verges on Blacks family.
HERMES GREY.differentiator: The darkest stone in the Greys family by visual reading — close to crossing into Blacks. White crackle is finer and denser than Daisy Grey's bold strokes; the base is much darker than Daisy Grey. Saint Laurent-related but with classic crackle vs Saint Laurent's sharper linear veins.

pattern.type: honey-amber field with cream cloud patches OR horizontal wave banding
pattern.vein_color: cream, pale peach, fine white crackle
pattern.vein_density: medium — variant-dependent: dense cream cloud patches in deep variant, pale horizontal waves in light variant

HONEY ONYX.visual_description: A translucent onyx in rich amber-honey orange, ranging from deep caramel-amber slabs with dramatic cream cloud patches (the signature look) to paler honey-peach variants with fine horizontal wave banding. The deep variant is the stone most buyers expect — saturated golden-orange with cloud-like cream interruptions and white crackle. Beautiful when backlit. The lighter variant is more restrained and reads as soft peach-cream with amber streaks.
HONEY ONYX.differentiator: Deep variant has the richest, most saturated amber-honey base in the family — Mango is peachier/lighter, Tiger is more tan with horizontal stripes, Medusa is matte golden-ochre (sandstone not onyx). The translucent crystalline body and dramatic cream cloud patches are the signatures. Backlit-appropriate, unlike Medusa Gold or Tiger Onyx.

pattern.type: cloudy with fine vein cracking

ICE BERG.visual_description: A cool light grey marble with horizontal grain movement and fine darker grey vein cracking. The icy cool tone matches its name — reads almost like frozen water or weathered stone. Cleaner and cooler than the warmer Bulberry/Celina greys.
ICE BERG.differentiator: The coolest, iciest grey in the family — much cooler-toned than the warm Bulberry/Celina greys. More directional grain than the cloud-only Grey Flurry. Bordering on the Whites family in lightness, but the cool grey cracking keeps it firmly in Greys.

color.secondary: sparse warm gold / amber hairline veins

pattern.vein_color: warm gold, amber, occasional cool grey
pattern.vein_density: low — sparse filaments on an icy-pure base

ICICLE ONYX.visual_description: A pure pale white-cream translucent onyx with a notably icy, glass-like clarity — the name 'Icicle' fits perfectly. Sparse warm gold and amber hairline veins thread softly diagonally across the slab, adding minimal pattern. The purest, most translucent onyx in the collection.
ICICLE ONYX.differentiator: Purest, coolest onyx in the Whites — most translucent and minimally-patterned. No coloured zones like Dragon Onyx or Pink Onyx, no warm waves like Cream Wave Onyx. Gold hairlines are very sparse.

color.accent: warm tobacco-brown undertones and fine white hairlines
