pattern.vein_color: medium grey, warm tobacco-brown, fine white diagonal hairlines

INDIAN TOBACCO.visual_description: A strongly directional marble with horizontal wood-grain banding in alternating dark grey-black and medium grey, punctuated by warm tobacco-brown undertones and thin diagonal white hairline veins. Reads visually as a 'dark striated' stone more than a true brown — the warmth comes from subtle tobacco undertones inside the grey bands rather than from a brown field.
INDIAN TOBACCO.differentiator: Strongly horizontal wood-grain banding with a grey-dark base and warm tobacco undertones. Reads darker and greyer than Tobacco Brown (which is rich chocolate-warm). The diagonal white hairlines cutting across the horizontal bands are a distinguishing feature.

pattern.type: dark charcoal base with horizontal grey-white wavy banding
pattern.vein_color: bright white, pale grey, warm gold

INFINITY.visual_description: A dark charcoal quartzite with dramatic horizontal grey-white wavy banding — like aerial view of mountain valleys or river cross-sections. Warm gold filaments add contrast accent.
INFINITY.differentiator: Dark charcoal with horizontal wavy grey-white banding — more dramatic than Ocean Wood's travertine banding, less directional than Silver Travertino.

pattern.type: stony crackle vein network with darker blue-grey shadow zones
pattern.vein_color: blue-grey, stony dark grey, fine white
pattern.vein_density: medium-dense — stony crackle pattern across a quiet grey-white base with darker shadow zones

INVICTUS.visual_description: A cool grey-white marble with a fine stony crackle veining and irregular darker blue-grey shadow zones that read almost like faded bruises on the stone. No warm accents — fully cool palette. The crackle is tighter and more 'stony' than Caspian's (less hairline, more textured), and there's no rust. Reads uniformly cool with a slight blue undertone.
INVICTUS.differentiator: Stony crackle + darker blue-grey shadow zones with NO warm/rust accents is the ID — Caspian has rust hairlines (Invictus has none), Invisible Blue has directional sweeps, Aquabella has horizontal waves. Fully cool palette is the tell.

color.accent: darker blue-grey shadow zones and warm gold/rust hairlines

pattern.type: sweeping diagonal flows of pale blue-grey with bright white directional streaks
pattern.vein_color: bright white, pale blue-grey, darker charcoal shadows, warm gold/rust hairlines
pattern.vein_density: medium — directional flow movement across a quiet blue-grey base

INVISIBLE BLUE.visual_description: A cool pale grey-blue marble with strong sweeping diagonal movement — bright white streaks flow across the slab against a softly blue-tinted grey base, with darker blue-grey shadow zones breaking up the directional sweep. Warm gold/rust hairlines add occasional contrast. The blue is subtle (hence 'invisible') — it reads as a cool grey marble with a blue cast rather than a saturated blue. Quiet, elegant, architectural.
INVISIBLE BLUE.differentiator: Strongly DIAGONAL sweeping movement sets it apart from other pale blue-grey marbles — Aquabella has horizontal waves (not diagonal), Azul Bahia here is blue-grey cloud swirls (not sweeping streaks), Caspian has crackle veining (not sweeps), Invictus has denser stony crackle. If it's pale blue-grey AND strongly diagonal, it's Invisible Blue.

color.accent: subtle olive-green hints and cream highlights

pattern.type: warm tan-beige with diagonal striated banding and subtle olive hints

IRISH VERDE.visual_description: A warm tan-beige marble with strongly diagonal striated banding and very subtle olive-green hints threading through. Despite 'Verde' (green) in the name, the stone reads predominantly as a warm beige with just faint olive undertones. Closer to Bulberry Beige or other warm beiges than any true green.
IRISH VERDE.differentiator: Warm tan-beige with diagonal striations and faint olive undertones — NOT visually green. The olive is very subtle; base dominates as beige. Diagonal direction distinguishes from cloudy beiges.

pattern.type: subtle wispy mineral threading across a natural-cleft surface

KANDLA BROWN.visual_description: A pale beige-tan Indian sandstone with a natural-cleft (rough riven) surface and soft, wispy pale-cream mineral marks tracing gently across the slab. The overall look is warm sand/tan — far lighter than any true brown marble and closer to a natural beige paving stone. Typically supplied as paving/cladding with a rustic texture rather than a polished finish.
KANDLA BROWN.differentiator: The only sandstone in the Browns family and the only stone with a natural-cleft rough surface — most Browns are polished marbles/quartzites. Much lighter than any true brown; sits at the beige-tan border. Paving/landscape use rather than interior feature surface.

color.secondary: dramatic cream-white crisscross crackle vein network
color.accent: fine darker charcoal hairlines and rust filaments

pattern.type: warm chocolate brown field with dense cream-white crisscross crackle vein network

LA TELLA.visual_description: A warm chocolate brown marble with dense cream-white crisscross crackle vein network spreading across the slab like tree branches. Warm-dark with dramatic veining — similar character to Tropical Storm but with denser cream crisscross.
LA TELLA.differentiator: Warm chocolate brown with dense cream crisscross crackle — sister to Tropical Storm (lattice) and French Brown (pebble), but with linear crisscross pattern.

pattern.type: pale grey field with soft cream-white cloudy drifts
pattern.vein_color: fine white hairlines, subtle darker grey

LAGOS.visual_description: A pale soft grey marble with gentle cream-white cloudy movement drifting diagonally. Very quiet — a background stone with subtle watercolor character. Similar to Pantheon and Dior Pearl in the whisper-quiet cloud-pattern marbles.
LAGOS.differentiator: Quiet pale grey with soft cloud movement — among the quietest stones in the collection. Lighter than Pantheon Grey, less speckled than Enigma.

pattern.type: horizontally banded

LASA COVELANO.visual_description: A warm-white Italian marble defined by pronounced horizontal wood-grain-like banding — cream, taupe, and pale grey layers flow across the slab in wavy parallel lines. Looks like a cross-section of carved wood or sedimentary layering. The banding is the hero feature.
LASA COVELANO.differentiator: Strong horizontal wood-grain banding is the unique signature — no other Whites family stone shows this directional striped pattern. Pantheon has some horizontal bands but they're softer and partial; Lasa Covelano is banded edge-to-edge. Completely different from its cousin Bianco Lasa which is a plain near-solid white.

color.accent: cream highlights and darker grey shadow zones

pattern.type: warm grey-brown field with dense reddish-brown hairline vein network

LAVANTO.visual_description: A warm grey-brown / taupe marble with a dense branching network of reddish-brown hairline veins. Similar character to Bulberry Beige (warm grey-brown with rust hairlines) but greyer/more neutral.
LAVANTO.differentiator: Warm grey-brown with dense rust hairline network — sister to Bulberry Beige but greyer. Not as warm-tan as pure Beiges, not as dark as Browns.

color.accent: white mineral veins and cream mottling

pattern.type: scattered gold pyrite flecks and white veins across royal blue base
pattern.vein_color: bright golden yellow (pyrite inclusions), white crystalline
pattern.vein_density: medium — flecks and white veins distributed across a dominantly-blue field

LAZURITE.visual_description: A deep royal-blue semi-precious stone slab with dramatic scattered clusters of bright golden-yellow pyrite flecks and white mineral veins drifting across the blue field. The blue is uniformly saturated (not patchy), and the pyrite gold reads as discrete flecks and small clusters rather than broad gold zones. One of the most collectible true-blue stones — used for high-end feature walls. Very close visual twin with Soda Lite Blue; the two need side-by-side inspection to separate.
LAZURITE.differentiator: Near-identical sister stone to Soda Lite Blue — BOTH are royal blue with golden pyrite flecks. Lazurite typically reads slightly more uniform blue with scattered discrete flecks; Sodalite tends to show more cream/white mottling interrupting the blue and patchier gold distribution. The lens should treat Lazurite and Sodalite as a paired-confusion cluster — physical side-by-side is often required to call. NOT similar to Vibranium (directional horizontal waves, no gold flecks) despite both being 'dark blue' stones.

color.accent: warm gold-bronze filaments and cream mineral veins

surface.texture: coarse crystalline with iridescent flash facets

pattern.type: dark crystalline field with scattered iridescent blue flash crystals
pattern.vein_color: iridescent blue (labradorescence), cream mineral hairlines, warm gold-bronze filaments
pattern.vein_thickness: crystal-sized flash patches (millimetre to centimetre scale)
pattern.vein_density: medium — iridescent flash scattered across the dark base, varying with viewing angle

LEMURIAN BLUE.visual_description: A dark charcoal-black labradorite granite with a scattered constellation of iridescent blue flash crystals (labradorescence / schiller) that catch light and glow blue when viewed at the right angle. Cream and warm gold-bronze mineral filaments weave through the dark base. The blue is NOT a uniform pigment — it is an optical flash effect that appears and disappears with viewing angle. Trade-called 'Lemurian Blue' but also known as Labradorite.
LEMURIAN BLUE.differentiator: Iridescent optical flash crystals on a dark granite base is unique in Blues — Lazurite/Sodalite have solid gold pyrite flecks (not iridescent), Vibranium has horizontal wave banding (not crystal flash). The blue visually appears/disappears with viewing angle — the hallmark of labradorite. Coarser crystalline texture than any other Blue.

pattern.type: fracture-veined (crackled)

LILAC WHITE.visual_description: A bright white marble with a dense, crackle-like web of lilac-purple veining spreading across the slab like frost on glass. The purple is clearly lavender — not grey and not brown — which is extraordinarily unusual for marble. Occasional soft gold hairlines appear between the lilac fractures.
LILAC WHITE.differentiator: Purple veining is the unique signature — no other stone in the Whites family has a true lilac hue. Pigus White has faint purple-grey hairlines but Lilac White is unmistakably lavender and much denser. Fracture web is similar in form to Bianco Eliptus but with purple where Eliptus has rust.

color.accent: silvery crystalline clusters and white hairlines

pattern.type: deep black field with bold diagonal bronze-gold streaks and silvery crystalline clusters
pattern.vein_thickness: variable (broad diagonal streaks and fine filaments)

LILI FUSION.visual_description: A deep-black granite with bold diagonal bronze-gold streaks slashing across the slab and silvery crystalline clusters adding texture. Near-cousin to Cosmic Gold (Blacks) but with bronze rather than pure gold, and more streaky than explosive.
LILI FUSION.differentiator: Deep black with diagonal BRONZE-gold streaks — more bronze/copper tone than Cosmic Gold (pure gold), more streaky-directional than Cosmic Gold (which explodes).

color.secondary: dense warm gold / rust branching vein network

pattern.type: bright white-cream field with dense warm gold/rust branching vein network
pattern.vein_color: warm gold-rust (dense branching), fine darker grey

LUMIX.visual_description: A bright white-cream quartzite with dense warm gold / rust-brown branching vein network spreading across the slab — similar to Calacatta Gold but more intensely warm-veined.
LUMIX.differentiator: Dense WARM gold-rust network on white — sister to Calacatta family but more warm-saturated vein colouring.

pattern.type: soft cloudy mottling with porous texture
pattern.vein_color: subtle darker grey flecks, pale cream highlights

LUSSO.visual_description: A soft warm grey-beige limestone with a gently mottled, slightly porous surface and quiet cream/grey variations. The base is a calm warm-neutral with very little directional movement — more a textural backdrop than a statement stone. Reads overall as beige-taupe; the brown undertone is subtle.
LUSSO.differentiator: Soft porous limestone with minimal pattern and a warm neutral field — the quietest stone in the Browns family. No veining, no wood grain, no crackle. The warm-neutral base with porous texture is the ID.

color.secondary: dramatic teal-green and dark charcoal diagonal streaks
color.accent: cream highlights and fine gold filaments

pattern.type: warm peach-beige base with dramatic teal-green and charcoal diagonal streaks
pattern.vein_thickness: variable (broad diagonal streaks and fine filaments)

LUXURIA.visual_description: A spectacular quartzite where a warm peach-beige base meets dramatic teal-green and dark charcoal diagonal streaks running across the slab. Bold warm-cool contrast with multiple visual zones. Sister in character to Pincelada but with peach-beige dominance.
LUXURIA.differentiator: Warm peach-beige with teal-green + charcoal diagonal streaks — sister to Pincelada (warmer, more orderly diagonal) and Forest Creek (horizontal not diagonal).

color.accent: warm pink-rose mortar traces and fine gold

pattern.type: large angular grey and white breccia fragments cemented with cream-pink mortar
pattern.vein_color: cream, pink-rose, fine gold, darker grey
pattern.vein_density: medium — fragment boundaries define the pattern

LYNX.visual_description: A breccia / agglomerate marble with LARGE angular grey and white marble fragments cemented together with cream-pink mortar and darker mineral pockets. Unique 'stone-cluster' look — completely different character from any flowing marble.
LYNX.differentiator: Breccia / agglomerate composition with large fragments — unique in the neutral family. If the slab looks like cemented rock pieces, it's Lynx.

pattern.type: diagonal streaky banding

MAGMA.visual_description: A dark brown-black Chinese quartzite with dramatic diagonal streaks of warm copper, tan, and silvery tones flowing across the slab like lava flows or wood grain seen through smoke. The warm brown-black base and copper veining suggest 'molten magma' — hence the name. More brown-warm than cool black; less dramatic than Cosmic Gold but with similar warm-accent character.
MAGMA.differentiator: Warm diagonal streaky banding (not explosive clusters like Cosmic Gold, not vertical hairlines like Nero Saint Laurent). Lighter and browner than the true blacks — sits at the warm/brown end of the Blacks family. Copper-tan accents rather than pure gold.

pattern.type: pebble/bubble-like translucent cloud pattern
pattern.vein_density: very dense — full-coverage pebble/bubble cell pattern

MANGO ONYX.visual_description: A warm peach-orange onyx with a highly distinctive pebble/bubble-like translucent cell pattern across the slab — like cross-sections of dried mango flesh. The tone leans peachier and more yellow-pink than Honey Onyx; pale mauve-pink ribbons occasionally thread through the pebbled orange field. The cellular texture is the strongest ID cue.
MANGO ONYX.differentiator: Pebble/bubble cellular texture is unique in the family — no other Orange has this across-the-slab cell pattern. Peachier and lighter than Honey Onyx; no horizontal banding like Tiger Onyx. Soft mauve-pink accents distinguish it from pure amber onyxes.

color.accent: cream-white hairlines and occasional copper flecks

pattern.type: fiery orange-red vein clusters on dark brown base
pattern.vein_thickness: thin to medium (vein clusters and branching filaments)
pattern.vein_density: medium-dense — dramatic fiery vein network across a dark brown field

MARCO POLO.visual_description: A dark rich-brown marble dramatically scored with fiery orange-red vein clusters that cut diagonally across the slab — the fiery veining is strikingly painterly, almost like molten copper pouring through dark rock. Cream-white hairlines add a secondary layer of vein work. One of the most visually dramatic browns in the collection.
MARCO POLO.differentiator: Fiery orange-red vein clusters are the signature — no other Brown stone has this level of dramatic red-copper veining. Darker chocolate base than Metal Rust with brighter orange (not rust-red) accents, and more dramatic clustering than Metal Rust's angular network.

pattern.type: cloudy mottled with white hairlines

MASA GREY.visual_description: A warm light grey marble with cloudy mottled depth and scattered white hairline veining. Reads as a softly textured beige-leaning grey — calm but with more visual movement than the very-uniform Grey Flurry.
MASA GREY.differentiator: Among the warm light greys (Bulberry, Celina, Sonata, Masa), Masa Grey shows the most pronounced cloudy mottling with visible white hairlines — neither as uniform as Grey Flurry nor as taupe-warm as Bulberry Grey.

surface.texture: natural sedimentary (soft horizontal layering, slightly porous)

pattern.type: soft horizontal sedimentary layering
pattern.vein_color: subtle darker amber and lighter tan horizontal bands
pattern.vein_density: medium — gentle full-coverage horizontal sediment pattern

MEDUSA GOLD.visual_description: A warm golden-ochre sandstone with soft sedimentary horizontal layering and a slightly porous, matte character. The base is a rich, earthy amber-gold — the most saturated of the 'warm earth' stones in the Oranges family. No crackle, no dramatic veining — just a consistently warm glowing golden field with gentle stratified direction. Reads as ochre rather than fire.
MEDUSA GOLD.differentiator: Matte natural sandstone (not polished onyx or quartzite) — the only sandstone in the Oranges family. Warm golden-ochre base without any dramatic pattern. Softer and less banded than Noche Travertino, less translucent than any onyx. If it's matte, warm-gold, and quiet, it's Medusa Gold.

color.accent: occasional darker charcoal clusters and fine white hairlines

pattern.type: rust-red angular vein network on warm brown base
pattern.vein_color: rust-red, copper, occasional dark charcoal, fine white
pattern.vein_thickness: hairline to medium (network of branching angular veins)
pattern.vein_density: medium-dense — rusting-metal network across the slab

METAL RUST.visual_description: A warm smoky-brown quartzite overlaid with a dramatic network of rust-red and copper veins branching angularly across the slab — the pattern evokes oxidized, rusting metal. The base brown is medium-dark and slightly cloudy; the rust-red veining is unmistakable and gives the stone its name. Darker charcoal clusters add depth.
METAL RUST.differentiator: Rust-red angular vein network is unique in the Browns family — no other Brown stone has copper-rust veining this prominent. Base is warm smoky brown (not chocolate), and the angular veins read as rusting metal rather than wood grain or crackle.

color.accent: bronze-gold crystal clusters and fine rust filaments

pattern.type: dark blue-black field with dense silvery-white crystalline flow pattern and bronze-gold clusters
pattern.vein_thickness: variable (broad flow patterns and fine filaments)

METALIKA.visual_description: A dark blue-black granite with dense silvery-white crystalline flow patterns swirling across the slab and bronze-gold crystal clusters adding warm metallic accent. The name fits — metallic, dramatic.
METALIKA.differentiator: Dark blue-black with flowing silver-white + bronze-gold — more flowing than Lili Fusion (diagonal streaks), cooler than Cosmic Gold (pure gold).

pattern.type: near-uniform with horizontal striations
pattern.vein_color: very faint warm cream and pale grey
pattern.vein_density: very sparse — directional grain rather than discrete veins

MOCCA CREAM.visual_description: A very pale cream limestone with subtle horizontal woodgrain-like striations. Reads almost as off-white with a soft warm tint. Lighter and more delicate than most beiges — the Mocca name refers to the soft coffee-cream color rather than dark mocca brown.
MOCCA CREAM.differentiator: Limestone (not marble), giving it a softer, more chalky look than the cream-beige marbles. Lighter and cooler than Fontana (which is warmer pink-peach) and more directional/grainy than the uniform Ottoman Beige. Despite the 'Mocca' name, it's a pale cream — not brown — making it one of the lightest stones in the Beiges family.

color.accent: olive-green shadows and occasional warm amber filaments

pattern.type: diagonal crystalline white streaks over a dark earth-brown base
pattern.vein_color: icy white (crystalline), olive-green shadows, warm amber filaments
pattern.vein_density: medium — dramatic diagonal streaks across the slab

MONT SIERRA.visual_description: A warm dark earth-brown quartzite with dramatic icy-white crystalline streaks cutting diagonally across the slab like glacial flows through a mountain face — hence the 'Mont Sierra' name. The base is warm earth-brown with subtle olive-green undertones, and the crystalline white streaks are the visual hero. More directional than Artico and darker than Fantasy Brown.
MONT SIERRA.differentiator: Diagonal icy-white crystalline streaks over warm dark earth-brown is unique in the family — no other Brown has this glacial-on-mountain look. Darker base than Artico and more directional streaking than Fantasy Brown's crackle.

pattern.type: diagonal wood-grain banding
pattern.vein_color: cream, beige, warm medium brown, darker charcoal
pattern.vein_density: dense — diagonal wood-grain stripe pattern across the slab

MORGANA.visual_description: A warm medium-brown marble with strong diagonal wood-grain banding in alternating warm brown, cream, and darker charcoal tones — like polished driftwood. The diagonal direction is the hallmark; the banding flows naturally from corner to corner. Reads warmer and lighter than Tobacco Brown, and decidedly more directional than Fantasy Brown's crackle.
MORGANA.differentiator: Diagonal wood-grain banding in warm medium brown — more diagonal than Tobacco Brown (horizontal) and warmer/lighter than Indian Tobacco (grey-dark). The driftwood-diagonal look is the signature.

pattern.type: scattered grey mineral flecks on pale cream-pink base
pattern.vein_color: soft grey flecks, occasional darker mineral spots
pattern.vein_density: low-medium — quiet field with scattered grey mineral speckling

MORINUS BLUE.visual_description: A pale cream-pink limestone with scattered grey mineral flecks drifting across the slab. The surface is slightly porous and matte, reading as a soft warm-neutral background stone. Has NO actual blue colouring visible — the 'Blue' in the name is a trade label that does not correspond to visual appearance. Closer to a pale beige/taupe limestone than any stone in the Blues family.
MORINUS BLUE.differentiator: Pale cream-pink limestone with grey flecks — DOES NOT READ AS BLUE AT ALL. The only stone in the Blues family with no visible blue colour. Lens should very strongly expect Beiges / Cream / Taupes matches rather than any Blues family match.

pattern.type: swirled marbling

NEBULA.visual_description: A dramatic white marble with flowing, liquid-like marbling of black, warm brown, and sage-green swirls that look like ink dropped into milk. The movement is fluid and abstract, reminiscent of paper marbling or a cosmic nebula — hence the name. Each slab is completely unique due to the chaotic flow pattern.
NEBULA.differentiator: Flowing, painterly swirled marbling is the unique signature — completely different from Dover White's discrete topographic pools (which are localized). Multi-color (black + brown + green) accents distinguish it from single-color-veined Calacattas. Motion is the defining quality — looks like liquid in motion, frozen.

pattern.type: sparse linear veining
pattern.vein_color: white hairlines with warm amber-gold streaks
pattern.vein_density: sparse — a few dramatic vertical streaks per slab

NERO SAINT LAURENT.visual_description: The iconic Tunisian black marble — a pitch-black base crossed by a small number of sharp vertical white hairline veins and distinctive warm amber-gold streaks running top to bottom. The gold streaks are the signature feature: bright copper-amber tones that contrast against the deep black field. Understated and dramatic at the same time.
NERO SAINT LAURENT.differentiator: Warm amber-gold streaks against pitch black are the signature — no other black in the family has this gold coloration at meaningful scale. Black Marquina has only white veins (no gold); Grey Saint Laurent is darker brown-grey rather than true pitch black; Cosmic Gold is more multicolor with dense gold bursts rather than sparse vertical streaks.

color.secondary: lighter tan bands and darker rust streaks
color.accent: cream highlights and occasional pore holes
color.shade: medium (ranges pale tan to rich amber)

pattern.type: horizontal vein-cut banding with porous travertine pitting
pattern.vein_color: warm honey, darker rust, cream highlights
pattern.vein_thickness: medium to broad parallel horizontal bands
pattern.vein_density: dense — full-coverage directional banding with natural pore texture

NOCHE TRAVERTINO.visual_description: A warm honey-amber travertine ranging from pale tan-beige slabs to richly saturated amber-rust variants, cut vein-direction so the strong horizontal banding dominates the visual. Distinctive natural pitting (open pores typical of travertine) interrupts the surface — sometimes filled for polish, often left open for rustic character. Warmer and more honey-toned than Ocean or Silver Travertino; this is the 'dark/warm' travertine in the family.
NOCHE TRAVERTINO.differentiator: Porous travertine texture with horizontal vein-cut banding in warm honey-amber is the ID — distinct from onyxes (which are translucent), from Medusa Gold (which is matte sandstone without pores), and from other travertines in the collection which are cooler silver or beige. Natural pores are the strongest tactile/visual cue. 'Noche' meaning 'night' in Spanish refers to the darker warm tone relative to cream travertines.

pattern.type: layered diagonal striations

OBSIDIAN.visual_description: A dramatic dark quartzite with flowing diagonal layered stripes of blue-grey, dark brown, rust, and black — reads like topographic rock layers frozen in motion. Despite the 'Obsidian' name (suggesting volcanic glass), the slab is actually a metamorphic quartzite with visible banded structure rather than a pure glassy black.
OBSIDIAN.differentiator: Dense diagonal layered striations in multiple dark tones — completely different from the crisp veined Blacks (Black Marquina, Nero Saint Laurent). Less uniform than Basaltino and more directional than Rivera Black's flowing streaks.

color.accent: darker grey pitting and rust accent

pattern.type: horizontal vein-cut banding with silvery grey and warm amber/tan
pattern.vein_thickness: medium to broad parallel horizontal bands
pattern.vein_density: dense — full-coverage horizontal banding with porous texture

OCEAN TRAVERTINO.visual_description: A silvery-grey / warm taupe travertine with strong horizontal vein-cut banding in alternating cool grey and warm amber/tan tones, interrupted by natural travertine pitting. Reads as a neutral-warm travertine — cooler than Noche Travertino (which is honey-amber), warmer than Silver Travertino (pure cool grey).
OCEAN TRAVERTINO.differentiator: Warm-cool mixed travertine — sits between Silver Travertino (pure cool grey) and Beige Travertino (warm tan). Horizontal vein-cut banding with porous texture is the travertine hallmark. Less honey than Noche Travertino.

color.secondary: dense horizontal wood-grain banding in grey and darker charcoal
color.accent: fine white and occasional rust hairlines

pattern.type: dense horizontal wood-grain banding in cool silvery-grey and charcoal
pattern.vein_color: cool grey, darker charcoal, fine white, occasional rust
pattern.vein_thickness: thin to medium parallel horizontal bands

OCEAN WOOD.visual_description: A cool silvery-grey travertine with deep blue-grey undertones and dense horizontal wood-grain banding that reads like polished driftwood in cool tones. Much darker and more directional than standard Silver Travertino — user-noted as near-identical to Silver Travertino. The cool horizontal banding is the hallmark.
OCEAN WOOD.differentiator: Darker silvery-grey with deep blue-grey undertones — near-identical to Silver Travertino per user observation. Ocean Wood tends to read slightly cooler and more blue-tinted; Silver Travertino is a pure cool grey. Strong horizontal wood-grain is shared.

pattern.type: cool white field with dense grey crackle vein network and warm rust accents

OMNI BIANCO.visual_description: A cool white marble with a dense network of grey crackle veins and fine warm rust-brown hairlines threading through. The name 'Omni Bianco' (all-white in Italian) fits — predominantly white with crackle movement.
OMNI BIANCO.differentiator: Cool white with dense grey crackle and rust hairlines — less dramatic than Twilight (black crackle), softer than Bianco Moronus.

pattern.type: web-veined

OPUS.visual_description: A soft warm-white quartzite with a delicate crisscrossing web of fine hairline veins tinted pale grey and amber-gold. The veining is subtle and elegant — not dramatic — giving the slab gentle movement without overwhelming the white field. Slightly warm overall glow.
OPUS.differentiator: Quartzite (not marble), so it has a crystalline translucency Bianco Vogue and Pantheon lack. Warmer amber-gold accents than Pigus White which leans cooler grey. Finer, more delicate web than Pirgon's bolder diagonal streaks.

pattern.type: crystalline / shattered glass

ORACLE GREY.visual_description: A cool light grey marble with a distinctive crystalline texture that reads like shattered glass or angular crystal facets across the slab. No defined veins — the visual interest comes from the fragmented mineral pattern. Cool, sophisticated, and unique.
ORACLE GREY.differentiator: Crystalline shattered-glass texture is the unique signature — completely different from the smooth cloudy or veined greys. Cooler than the warm Bulberry/Celina/Masa greys and more textured than the uniform Grey Flurry.

pattern.type: breccia / terrazzo pebble

OREO GREY.visual_description: A bright cream-white marble with a dramatic terrazzo / breccia texture made up of irregular angular pebble pieces in shades of grey, dark grey, and occasional black inclusions. The 'Oreo' name comes from the cream + dark contrast — like a scattered Oreo cookie pattern.
OREO GREY.differentiator: Cream-white base distinguishes it from Grey Williams (which has a darker grey base for the same pebbled style). The terrazzo / pebble pattern with sharp angular pieces is the unique character — far more textural than the smooth/cloudy greys.

pattern.type: near-uniform with fine speckling

OTTOMAN BEIGE.visual_description: A pale cream-beige marble with very fine pinpoint speckling and almost no visible veining. Reads as nearly solid warm cream-beige with a soft texture. Calm, uniform, and easy on the eye.
OTTOMAN BEIGE.differentiator: Among the uniform Beiges, Ottoman Beige stands out for its fine pinpoint speckled texture (rather than smooth field). Lacks the vein lines of Crema Marfil/Crema Uno and the mottled cloudy zones of Bianco Siena. The most 'particle-textured' uniform beige in the family.

color.accent: dark grey-bronze spotted clusters and warm bronze veining

pattern.type: swirling painterly flow with dark bronze/grey clusters
pattern.vein_color: soft green-teal, warm bronze, dark grey-black
pattern.vein_density: medium — painterly flows with scattered dark clusters

PALISSANDRO BRONZO.visual_description: A cream-white Italian marble with sweeping painterly flows of soft teal-green and dark bronze-grey veining, punctuated by dense irregular clusters of dark grey-black spotting. The 'bronzo' in the name refers to the warm bronze accents in the vein work, but the slab reads overall as a light, pale, green-accented marble rather than a true brown stone.
PALISSANDRO BRONZO.differentiator: Named 'Bronzo' for its bronze vein accents but visually very light — cream base with teal-green flows is the dominant read. Darker spotted clusters distinguish it from pure cream Palissandros. The lens should expect Whites / Greens confusion.

color.secondary: vibrant gold, rust-orange, and peach-coral zones

pattern.type: warm grey field with vibrant gold, rust-orange, and peach-coral painterly zones
pattern.vein_color: warm gold, rust-orange, peach-coral, dark charcoal, white

PALLADIO.visual_description: A dramatic quartzite with warm grey base meeting vibrant gold, rust-orange, and peach-coral painterly zones, punctuated by white crystalline clusters and dark charcoal shadows. A spectacular collector's multi-color stone.
PALLADIO.differentiator: Warm grey with vibrant gold + rust + peach — more warm-toned than Pincelada (teal), warmer still than Palladio Gold variants.

pattern.type: cloudy flowing

PANDA WHITE.visual_description: A bright white marble with soft grey cloudy movement flowing across the slab like watercolor washes. Gentle, organic patterns — no sharp veins, just soft gradations of pale grey blending into the white base. Calm and subtly dynamic.
PANDA WHITE.differentiator: Cloudy grey is the softest-edged in the Whites family — no defined vein lines, just watercolor gradations. Contrast with Bianco Vogue (which has defined hairline veins) and Pantheon (horizontal bands). Not as uniform as Dior Pearl but far softer than Statuario.

pattern.type: banded and veined
pattern.vein_density: moderate — concentrated in horizontal bands with calm zones between

PANTHEON.visual_description: A bright white marble with a signature split personality — one half of the slab stays clean white while the other shows soft horizontal layered grey banding with occasional amber-gold hairlines. Creates a half-calm / half-active composition that's ideal for book-matched installations.
PANTHEON.differentiator: Half-calm, half-banded composition is the unique signature — unlike Lasa Covelano which is banded edge-to-edge, and unlike Bianco Vogue which has banding centered. Allows more clean white real estate than most Whites, which is valuable for large installations.

pattern.type: horizontally banded with grey-cream alternation

PANTHEON (GREY-LEANING SLABS).visual_description: The grey-dominant slabs from the Pantheon marble family. While the white-leaning Pantheon slabs (covered in the Whites family) show clean white with partial grey banding, the grey-leaning slabs are dominated by warm horizontal grey banding with smaller cream zones. Both come from the same Pantheon material — different slabs simply lean white or grey depending on the cut.
PANTHEON (GREY-LEANING SLABS).differentiator: Cross-family variant — same physical material as Pantheon (in Whites) but describing the grey-dominant slabs. The signature horizontal banding is shared with Lasa Covelano (also a Whites cross-variant candidate). Lighter and more cream-warm than the cool Bulberry Grey or Carrara Grey.

pattern.type: dramatic painterly fire-and-black composition — orange-copper meeting charcoal-black
pattern.vein_color: fiery copper-orange, dark charcoal, bronze-gold, cream
pattern.vein_thickness: variable (broad painterly zones and fine filaments)
pattern.vein_density: dense — full-coverage dramatic multi-color painterly movement

PARQUET.visual_description: A spectacular painterly quartzite where fiery copper-orange zones meet dark charcoal-black areas in dramatic brushstroke-like swirls, highlighted by cream-white patches and bronze-gold filaments. Among the most visually intense stones in the collection — user-confirmed as NOT orange family (it's too multi-color and dark-dominant for pure Oranges). Sits in Exotic / Multicolor.
PARQUET.differentiator: Dramatic orange-and-black painterly composition — MORE black-zone dominant than Fuego (which splits orange/white), no cool teal like Pincelada. If the slab is fire-orange meeting charcoal-black, it's Parquet.

color.accent: scattered warm amber and grey crystalline clusters
