pattern.vein_color: dark black branching, warm amber clusters
pattern.vein_density: dense — full-coverage branching black vein network

PATAGONIA.visual_description: A bright white-cream granite with dense black branching vein network and scattered warm amber and grey crystalline clusters. Classic Brazilian Patagonia granite — high-contrast white-and-black with warm mineral accents.
PATAGONIA.differentiator: Bright white with dense BLACK branching veins — high-contrast. More dramatic vein network than Alaska White, more structured than Genesis's speckle pattern.

color.secondary: cream-white and dark charcoal sweeping zones
color.accent: pink-mauve pockets and fine gold filaments

pattern.type: dark olive-green base with cream-white, charcoal, and pink-mauve mixed painterly zones
pattern.vein_color: cream-white, pink-mauve, dark charcoal, fine gold

PATANAL.visual_description: A complex multi-color quartzite blending dark olive-green, cream-white, dark charcoal, and pink-mauve in swirling painterly zones with fine gold filaments. Multi-tonal exotic — reads as a collector stone with no single dominant colour.
PATANAL.differentiator: Olive-green + cream + charcoal + pink-mauve painterly mix — more olive-dominant than Pincelada (teal-blue), mauve accents distinct.

color.accent: darker charcoal shadows and fine rust

pattern.type: white-cream base with swirling grey movement and warm peach-copper accents
pattern.vein_color: grey swirls, warm peach-copper, fine rust

PATINA.visual_description: A white-cream quartzite with dramatic swirling grey movement and warm peach-copper accent zones — the name 'Patina' (aged surface) fits the weathered, layered look.
PATINA.differentiator: White-cream base with swirling grey + peach-copper — softer than Pincelada (bolder teal), warmer than pure grey swirl marbles.

color.primary: pale cream-white with faint peach tint

pattern.type: pale near-white field with faint peach tint and diagonal warm gold/rust hairline veins
pattern.vein_density: low — sparse hairlines on a quiet pale base

PEACH ONYX.visual_description: A very pale near-white translucent onyx with a faint peach tint and sparse warm gold/rust hairline veins drifting diagonally across the slab. The peach is barely present — this reads almost as a Cream-Ivory onyx with warm gold accents. Quiet, elegant, minimally-patterned.
PEACH ONYX.differentiator: Palest in the Pinks/Reds — reads almost white/cream with faint peach. Much less saturated than Valle Rossa (pastel-but-visible pink) and Pink Onyx (distinct pink with orange band). Translucent onyx with quiet gold hairlines.

color.accent: darker black shadows and fine white hairlines

pattern.type: dark brown/charcoal base with cream and sandy-tan sweeping painterly flows
pattern.vein_color: cream, sandy-tan, dark charcoal, fine white

PHANTUS HYDRO.visual_description: A dark brown / charcoal quartzite with cream and sandy-tan painterly flows sweeping across the slab — like rivers through dark soil. Warm-dark multi-tonal. Sister character to exotic painterly quartzites but brown-dominant.
PHANTUS HYDRO.differentiator: Dark brown with cream painterly flows — less dramatic than Marco Polo (fiery red veins), more directional than Fantasy Brown (muted crackle).

pattern.type: grey-green painterly swirls with cream-white zones and warm gold-orange clusters
pattern.vein_color: grey-green, cream-white, warm gold-orange, dark charcoal

PICO DORADO.visual_description: A complex quartzite where grey-green painterly swirls dominate with cream-white zones and warm gold-orange mineral clusters adding warm accents. Multi-tonal — name means 'golden peak' in Spanish. Sister to Patanal in exotic multi-color character.
PICO DORADO.differentiator: Grey-green dominant with cream + gold-orange — more green-dominant than Patanal (olive), less teal than Pincelada.

color.accent: minimal tan and darker brown shadow

pattern.type: warm leather-brown field with subtle horizontal wavy grain
pattern.vein_color: subtle tan and darker brown shadows

PIETRA FINNO.visual_description: A warm leather-like brown marble with very subtle horizontal wavy grain and almost no veining. Reads as a pure warm brown surface — quiet, textural, minimalist. Among the quietest browns in the collection.
PIETRA FINNO.differentiator: Among the quietest browns — minimal pattern, soft leather-like surface. Contrast with Fantasy Brown (which has gold crackling).

pattern.type: veined (fine diagonal)
pattern.vein_color: cool grey with faint lilac undertones

PIGUS WHITE.visual_description: A bright white marble with fine diagonal grey hairline veining that has a subtle cool-lilac undertone on close inspection. The veining is elegant and linear, spreading diagonally across the slab like delicate brush strokes. Reads as a refined, slightly cooler cousin to Carrara.
PIGUS WHITE.differentiator: Faint lilac tint in the grey veins — much more subtle than Lilac White (which is overtly purple) but cooler and slightly purpler than other cloud-veined whites. Diagonal linear veins rather than Bianco Vogue's horizontal band or Opus's web pattern.

pattern.type: dramatic painterly multi-color zones with teal-blue, copper-orange, rust, grey, and cream flows
pattern.vein_thickness: variable (broad painterly zones and fine filaments)
pattern.vein_density: dense — full-coverage dramatic colour transitions across the slab

PINCELADA.visual_description: A spectacular multi-colour painterly quartzite — cream-white zones meeting bold teal-blue pockets, copper-orange and rust painterly flows, grey shadow zones, and dark charcoal pockets all swirling dramatically across the slab like an abstract painting. The name 'Pincelada' ('brushstroke' in Spanish) fits perfectly. No dominant single colour — Exotic/Multicolor territory.
PINCELADA.differentiator: Dramatic multi-colour painterly composition with no dominant single colour — teal + copper + rust + cream + grey all co-present. Closest relatives are the dramatic orange/cool quartzites (Fuego splits orange/white, Tramonto is sunset arcs, Emerald Flame has teal+copper). Pincelada has MORE colours than any of those; it's a collector piece.

pattern.type: bi-color banded — cream-white upper, orange-caramel translucent middle ribbon, soft pink lower with white crackle
pattern.vein_color: bright white crackle (lower), warm caramel translucent (middle)
pattern.vein_thickness: medium horizontal band layers with fine white crackle in the pink zones
pattern.vein_density: medium — distinct horizontal bands with crackle in the pink portions

PINK ONYX.visual_description: A distinctively bi-color onyx with three horizontal zones: cream-white at the top, a dramatic orange-caramel translucent ribbon through the middle, and soft pink with white crackle at the bottom. The orange-caramel band is the most arresting feature — it catches light when backlit. Reads as 'pink onyx with orange ribbon'.
PINK ONYX.differentiator: Tri-band composition (cream / orange ribbon / pink crackle) is unique — no other stone in Pinks has this horizontal 3-zone structure. Translucent onyx, backlit-ready. Cross-family: the orange ribbon suggests Oranges affiliation.

pattern.type: salmon-pink field with warm yellow-gold accents and darker pink crackle veins
pattern.vein_color: darker rust-pink, warm yellow-gold, occasional fine white
pattern.vein_density: medium-dense — full-coverage crackle network with warm accent clusters

PINK VALENCIA.visual_description: A salmon-pink / dusty rose marble with warm yellow-gold accent clusters and a crackle vein network of darker rust-pink hairlines. Warmer and more saturated than Valle Rossa (which is pastel), pinker than Red Verona (which is terracotta). Sits between a true pink marble and an apricot-peach stone.
PINK VALENCIA.differentiator: Salmon-pink with warm yellow-gold accents and crackle — warmer and more saturated than Valle Rossa (pastel quartzite), pinker than Red Verona (terracotta), more crackly than Pink Onyx (banded).

color.accent: darker grey and warm tan mineral fragments

pattern.type: grey pebble-cluster composition with cream mortar and darker fragments

PIOLINI.visual_description: A grey breccia / 'pebble-beach' agglomerate stone with mottled grey pebbles cemented in cream mortar and darker grey and warm tan mineral fragments. Like a polished cross-section of river rocks.
PIOLINI.differentiator: Pebble-cluster composition — smaller fragments than Lynx (large marble pieces), cooler-grey than Breccia Aura (warm beige).

pattern.type: streaked and veined

PIRGON.visual_description: A warm bright-white Greek marble with diagonal streaks of pale grey highlighted by amber-rust hairline veining. The overall tone is softly warm, and the veining feels organic and directional. Quarried from Pirgon (Greece), it has a slightly creamy luminosity.
PIRGON.differentiator: Warmer creamier tone than the pure-white Thassos (its Greek neighbor) with more visible amber-rust veining. More diagonal and streaky than Opus's fine web. Less yellow than Crystal Yellow Onyx, less dramatic than any Calacatta.

color.accent: occasional pink-rose mineral filaments and darker amber pockets

pattern.type: warm yellow-gold field with fine white crackle vein network and pink-rose mineral filaments
pattern.vein_color: fine white crackle, pink-rose, darker amber
pattern.vein_density: medium — full-coverage fine crackle on a warm yellow-gold base

PLATINUM GOLD.visual_description: A warm yellow-gold / giallo marble with a fine white crackle vein network spreading across the slab and occasional pink-rose mineral filaments. Classic 'Giallo' yellow marble palette — Italian heritage warm-gold character.
PLATINUM GOLD.differentiator: Warm yellow-gold marble with fine white crackle — the classic Italian giallo. No horizontal banding like onyxes, not sandstone-matte like Medusa Gold.

color.secondary: dramatic vertical rose-red and rust-orange hairlines

pattern.type: warm grey-taupe field with dramatic vertical rose-red and rust-orange hairline veins

POCCACHE.visual_description: A warm grey-taupe marble with dramatic VERTICAL rose-red and rust-orange hairline veins streaming down the slab. The vertical direction is distinctive — most marbles have horizontal or diagonal veining.
POCCACHE.differentiator: Warm grey-taupe with VERTICAL rose-red hairlines — the vertical direction and rose accent set it apart from Lavanto (horizontal rust) and Ancora (plum-dominant).

surface.grain_direction: strongly horizontal with diagonal vein filaments

pattern.type: dark grey-black field with cream-white horizontal bands and warm gold-rust diagonal filaments
pattern.vein_thickness: medium horizontal bands with fine diagonal filaments
pattern.vein_density: dense — full-coverage horizontal banding with diagonal accents

POLARIS.visual_description: A dark grey-black marble with cream-white horizontal stripes and warm gold-rust diagonal vein filaments cutting through. Dramatic wood-grain horizontal character with warm accent crossings.
POLARIS.differentiator: Dark grey-black with cream horizontal stripes and gold-rust diagonals — similar to Corteccia but greyer-black and more striped.

color.accent: pink-rose flecks and fine gold filaments

pattern.type: warm tan-beige painterly swirls with cream, olive-green, and pink-rose accents

POLURRIAN.visual_description: A complex multi-color quartzite blending warm tan-beige swirls with cream-white patches, olive-green undertones, and pink-rose flecks, all in painterly sweeping movement. Soft multi-tonal — reads warm-neutral with multi-color accents. Sister in character to Artico (Browns) and Patanal.
POLURRIAN.differentiator: Warm-neutral painterly multi-color with olive-green accents — sister to Artico but more painterly/swirled and with more olive.

color.primary: icy blue-grey and warm tan-peach zones
color.secondary: dark charcoal and green mineral shadows
color.accent: cream highlights and fine gold filaments

pattern.type: dramatic painterly composition with icy-blue upper zones meeting warm tan-peach lower zones
pattern.vein_color: icy blue-grey, warm tan-peach, dark charcoal, green mineral, gold
pattern.vein_thickness: variable (broad painterly zones and fine filaments)

PUNTELLO.visual_description: A dramatic quartzite where icy blue-grey sweeping flows dominate the upper half of the slab while warm tan-peach zones take over the lower half, punctuated by dark charcoal shadows and green mineral pockets. Fine gold filaments thread through. Visually a warm-cool contrast exotic stone — like meeting of sky and earth.
PUNTELLO.differentiator: Two-tone warm-cool composition (icy blue + warm tan-peach) is distinctive — similar character to Pincelada but simpler palette (two zones rather than many), more blue-warm contrast than Fuego (orange/white split).

color.accent: occasional grey mineral pockets and darker rust shadows

pattern.type: dense branching white vein network on terracotta orange-red field
pattern.vein_density: dense — full-coverage white vein network against saturated terracotta

RED ALIKANTE.visual_description: A saturated terracotta orange-red Spanish marble scored with a dense branching network of bright white veins that spreads across the slab like crazing glaze on pottery. The base ranges from warm coral-orange to deep brick-red terracotta depending on the slab, but the stone always reads strongly orange-warm rather than true cool red. Trade-named 'Red / Rojo Alicante' but visually unmistakably orange.
RED ALIKANTE.differentiator: Dense white crazing vein network on warm terracotta-orange base is the signature — no other Orange has this across-the-slab white crackle, and no other terracotta marble is this saturated orange-warm. Often catalogued with Reds, but sits in Oranges on visual color alone.

pattern.type: wine-red field with bright white branching veins and rust-orange striations
pattern.vein_color: bright white, warm rust-orange, occasional dark charcoal
pattern.vein_density: medium — crisp branching white veins against a saturated wine base

RED LAVANTE.visual_description: A classic deep wine / burgundy-red marble scored with a network of bright white branching veins and interrupted by warm rust-orange striations running diagonally across the slab. The red is rich and saturated — the classic Italian 'rosso' palette. Near-twin with Rosso Lavante (both 'Lavante' named) but differentiated by vein density and tone.
RED LAVANTE.differentiator: Near-twin with Rosso Lavante — BOTH are wine-red with white veins. Red Lavante tends to read slightly LIGHTER and more orange-tinted with rust striations and crisper branching white veins; Rosso Lavante is DEEPER burgundy with denser crackle network and less rust. If the slab has rust-orange striations, it's Red Lavante; if dense white crackle without rust, Rosso Lavante.

pattern.type: warm terracotta field with fine white hairline veins and dark mineral pockets
pattern.vein_density: low-medium — scattered hairlines on a uniformly warm field

RED VERONA.visual_description: A warm terracotta-red / rusty orange-red marble with fine white hairline veins and occasional dark charcoal mineral pockets. The base reads distinctly warmer and more orange than Red Lavante — sits between Reds and Oranges on the color spectrum. The classic Italian 'Rosso Verona' — a heritage favourite.
RED VERONA.differentiator: Warmer and MORE ORANGE-RED than Red/Rosso Lavante (which are wine-deep-red). Sparser hairlines — no dense crackle like Rosso Lavante. Borders the Oranges family; Red Alikante in Oranges is a close cross-family twin. If the slab reads orange-red with sparse white hairlines, it's Red Verona.

pattern.type: streaky / flowing vein network
pattern.vein_color: silver-white with occasional pale blue shimmer

RIVERA BLACK.visual_description: A deep blue-tinged black phyllite with dramatic silver-white streaky veining flowing diagonally across the slab like rain or cosmic star trails. The phyllite composition gives the stone a slight pearlescent shimmer and subtle blue undertone against the black. More flowing and directional than the crisp veining of Black Marquina.
RIVERA BLACK.differentiator: Phyllite (not marble) — gives it a slight pearlescent shimmer marbles lack, plus subtle blue undertone. Flowing/streaky veining is more directional than the crisp crackle of Black Marquina, and much denser than Nero Saint Laurent's sparse vertical streaks.

color.secondary: dense bright white crackle vein network

pattern.type: deep burgundy field with dense white crackle vein network and dark green mineral pockets
pattern.vein_color: bright white (dense branching crackle), dark green-black mineral
pattern.vein_density: dense — full-coverage crackle network across a deep wine-red base

ROSSO LAVANTE.visual_description: A deep burgundy / oxblood-red marble with a dense network of bright white crackle veins spreading across the slab like crazed porcelain, interrupted by occasional dark green-black mineral pockets. Deeper and more saturated than Red Lavante, with denser crackle veining and no rust striations. The classic 'Rosso' benchmark for deep red crackle marble.
ROSSO LAVANTE.differentiator: Near-twin with Red Lavante. Rosso Lavante is DEEPER burgundy with denser white crackle (no rust-orange striations). Red Lavante has rust-orange striations and crisper branching veins. If the slab reads oxblood-red with crackle-porcelain veining, it's Rosso Lavante.

pattern.type: horizontal linear striations (fabric-weave)

SILVER POTRO.visual_description: A very dark charcoal-black marble dramatically streaked with continuous silver-white horizontal lines that look like rain falling, fabric weave, or wet asphalt under streetlights. Very directional and graphic. Among the darkest stones in the Greys family.
SILVER POTRO.differentiator: Strongly horizontal silver-line striations are unique — completely different from Hermes Grey's white crackle web or Grey Saint Laurent's branching lightning. Sister stone to the lighter Silver Serpegiantte but much darker. Among the darkest stones in Greys; verges on Blacks.

pattern.type: horizontally banded (Serpeggiante / wood-vein)

SILVER SERPEGIANTTE.visual_description: A warm beige-grey limestone with strong horizontal Serpeggiante-style banding — wavy parallel layers of tan and brown across the slab like wood grain or sedimentary layers. Despite the 'Silver' name, the dominant impression is warm tan-beige rather than cool silver-grey.
SILVER SERPEGIANTTE.differentiator: Strong horizontal Serpeggiante (wood-grain) banding is the signature — different from any other Grey in the family. Despite the 'Silver' name, leans warm beige-tan rather than cool silver — visually borders the Beiges family.

pattern.type: horizontally banded (travertine layers)

SILVER TRAVERTINO.visual_description: A warm pale beige-grey travertine with strong horizontal layered banding in amber and tan tones with occasional grey streaks. Despite the 'Silver' name, the dominant impression is warm Tuscan beige rather than cool silver — though some bands do read as silver-grey. Italian travertine character.
SILVER TRAVERTINO.differentiator: True travertine in the Greys family — porous texture with strong horizontal banding distinguishes it from smooth marble greys. Lighter and warmer than the much-darker Grey Travertino. Italian-Roman style. Despite 'Silver' in the name, leans warmer beige than true cool silver-grey.

pattern.type: royal blue base with patchy cream-white mottling and gold pyrite clusters
pattern.vein_color: golden yellow pyrite, cream-white, occasional darker grey
pattern.vein_density: medium-dense — patchier and more interrupted than Lazurite

SODA LITE BLUE (SODALITE).visual_description: A deep royal-blue semi-precious sodalite slab with golden pyrite clusters and more prominent cream-white mottling interrupting the blue field than its Lazurite counterpart. The blue reads patchier here — the white and cream sections break up the blue into zones rather than flecks on a uniform field. Gold clusters tend to concentrate in patches rather than scatter evenly. Near-identical twin to Lazurite and easily confused with it.
SODA LITE BLUE (SODALITE).differentiator: Near-identical sister stone to Lazurite — BOTH are royal blue with pyrite gold. Sodalite typically shows MORE cream-white mottling breaking up the blue and patchier/clustered gold distribution; Lazurite reads more uniformly blue with finer scattered gold flecks. Physical side-by-side comparison is often needed; the white mottling is the strongest tie-breaker. NOT similar to Vibranium (different pattern entirely).

pattern.type: subtly veined with amber accents

SONATA GREY.visual_description: A warm light grey marble with cream undertones and scattered amber-rust hairline veining. The veining is subtle but adds a warm sparkle to the otherwise calm grey field. One of the warmest, lightest greys.
SONATA GREY.differentiator: Among the warm light greys (Bulberry, Celina, Masa, Sonata), Sonata Grey has the most visible amber-rust hairline accents — gives it a slightly warmer / more 'character' feel than the more uniform Bulberry or Grey Flurry.

pattern.type: cloudy / soft watercolor

SPIDER BEIGE.visual_description: A pale pink-beige marble with soft watercolor-like cloudy movement spread across the slab. The pink-warm undertone gives it a delicate, almost rose-cream feel. Calm and gentle, with diffuse cloud zones rather than sharp veins.
SPIDER BEIGE.differentiator: A soft pink-cream cloudy marble with diffuse watercolor-style washes — no defined vein lines or crackle network. Pinker base than Crema Marfil and softer/more diffuse than the linear veining of Crema Uno. Cloud movement is gentler than the breccia network of Crema Elysee.

pattern.type: veined (iconic Italian)
pattern.vein_color: cool grey with occasional warm amber
pattern.vein_density: moderate — distinctive signature grey veining with clean white zones

STATUARIO.visual_description: The iconic Italian white marble with a brilliant bright white base and distinctive cool grey veining that ranges from fine crackle networks to bold sweeping strokes. Occasional warm amber highlights appear at vein intersections. Legendary stone of classical sculpture (Michelangelo's David). Clean, prestigious, crisp.
STATUARIO.differentiator: Extremely close to Carrara (both are cool white Italian marbles with grey veining from the same mountain region) — the key separator is that Statuario has a BRIGHTER, WHITER base and BOLDER, MORE DEFINED grey veins with occasional warm amber highlights, while Carrara has more evenly-distributed fine hairline veins on a slightly duller cool-white base and no gold accents. Statuario is the premium sibling; Carrara is the everyday classic. Cleaner white than Bianco Lasa (cloudier) and Calacatta Caldiya (denser vein concentration). Grey-veined, unlike Calacatta Makia Vakia where gold dominates.

pattern.type: dense crackle / fracture veining
pattern.vein_density: dense — branching crackle across entire surface

STATUARIO BARATTINI.visual_description: A cool light-grey marble with a dense branching crackle network of dark charcoal veining spreading across the slab like cracked porcelain or tree branches. Shares the crisp Statuario character but on a distinctly grey base rather than pristine white, with darker and more branched veining. Reads as a dramatic grey cousin to the Italian Statuario family.
STATUARIO BARATTINI.differentiator: The grey sibling of the classic Statuario — shares the dramatic crackle/fracture vein character of Statuario (in Whites family) but on a cool grey base rather than bright white. Darker and denser veining than Carrara Grey (which has softer crackle on a lighter base). Less bold than Daisy Grey (which has thick white veins on darker grey); here the veins are the darker element against a lighter grey. Cooler than the blue-tinged Grey Bardilo.

pattern.type: spider-web / crackle vein network
pattern.vein_density: dense — extensive branching crackle network across the surface

SUPERIO BEIGE.visual_description: A pale cream-beige marble overlaid with a distinctive web-like network of darker amber-tan veining that branches and crackles across the slab like a spider-web stretched over the field. The web is the dominant visual feature — bold, organic, and architectural.
SUPERIO BEIGE.differentiator: The signature spider-web crackle vein pattern is the unique feature — finer and more web-like than the breccia network of Crema Elysee, and far more pronounced than the delicate crackling of Crema Purrisima. A different stone from Superior Beige (despite similar names) — Superio shows the strong web pattern; Superior shows discrete amber vein clusters.

pattern.type: veined with amber clusters
pattern.vein_density: moderate — clustered concentrations across the slab

SUPERIOR BEIGE.visual_description: A pale cream-beige marble with prominent rust-amber vein clusters that branch and run across the slab in defined lines (rather than a fine web). The veins are like cracked porcelain — dramatic, linear, and concentrated. Warm cream base shows soft horizontal grain underlying the vein pattern.
SUPERIOR BEIGE.differentiator: Different stone from Superio Beige (per user confirmation): Superior shows discrete rust-amber vein clusters and linear branching, while Superio Beige has a fine spider-web crackle. Superior's veining is bolder, less networked, more like classic Carrara-style cracking applied to a beige base.

pattern.type: banded and veined
pattern.vein_density: moderate — horizontal bands with amber streaks

TAJ MAHAL.visual_description: A luminous warm cream quartzite with horizontal golden-brown banding and amber veining. Depending on slab, ranges from cool-white with sparse gold streaks to strongly banded warm beige with chaotic crinkled topographic patterning. The crystalline structure gives a soft backlit glow. Serene, warm, natural.
TAJ MAHAL.differentiator: Warmer golden undertone than any marble white — the quartzite composition and crystalline translucency set it apart from Statuario, Bianco Lasa, and other marbles. Amber banding is softer and more flowing than Lasa Covelano's crisp horizontal bands. More golden and warmer than the pale cream Crystal Yellow Onyx.

pattern.type: cloudy stormy swirls
pattern.vein_color: soft grey-taupe with warm brown edges
pattern.vein_density: medium — large sweeping cloud-like movements across a cream field

TEMPEST.visual_description: A cream-white marble overlaid with soft stormy swirls of warm grey-taupe that sweep across the slab like cloud cover before a storm — hence 'Tempest'. The base is distinctly cream-warm rather than cool white, and the swirls carry brown undertones which place it at the very light end of the Browns family. Looks near-identical to Ammazza — the two are often paired as sister stones.
TEMPEST.differentiator: Among the lightest stones in the Browns family. Sweeping cloud-storm swirls (not tight crackle, not wood-grain). Near-identical to Ammazza — the two need their physical slabs side-by-side to tell apart. Warmer / creamier base than any grey storm marble.

pattern.type: solid / uniform

THASSOS.visual_description: The purest white marble in the world — a uniform, near-solid snow-white slab with almost zero veining or pattern. Quarried on the Greek island of Thassos, it reads as an absolute white with a faint crystalline glow. The benchmark pure-white reference stone.
THASSOS.differentiator: The purest, whitest stone in the Whites family — absolute zero veining. Cleaner, cooler, and whiter than Vietnam White (which has a faint warmth) and Dior Pearl (which has a pearl undertone). The gold-standard reference for 'pure white marble.'

color.shade: neutral (cool base with tiny warm accents)

pattern.type: near-solid with whisper veins

THASSOS NOVELATO.visual_description: A near-pure Thassos variant with a whisper of warm gold hairline veining running loosely through the otherwise pristine white field. The gold is so faint it almost reads as a warm shimmer rather than vein lines. Thassos's minimalist spirit with just a touch of warmth.
THASSOS NOVELATO.differentiator: The sister of pure Thassos with the faintest warm gold accenting — the key distinction is whether you see faint warm vein lines (Novelato) or absolutely none (pure Thassos). Warmer undertone than pure Thassos and much more subtle than any of the veined Calacattas or Statuario.

color.primary: pale near-white with subtle pistachio / celadon tint

pattern.type: pale near-white field with subtle pistachio tint and fine diagonal darker-grey veins
pattern.vein_color: fine darker grey, pink-rose filament, occasional amber
pattern.vein_density: low — quiet pattern on a pale base

TIFFANY.visual_description: A very pale near-white quartzite with a subtle pistachio / celadon green tint and fine diagonal darker-grey veins. Occasional pink-rose filaments add warm accent. Very quiet — among the whitest stones with just a whisper of green.
TIFFANY.differentiator: Pale near-white with subtle pistachio tint and fine diagonal veins — whispers of green distinguish from pure Thassos white.

color.accent: cream highlights and fine white hairlines

pattern.type: horizontal wood-grain / tiger-stripe banding
pattern.vein_color: darker amber stripes, cream highlights, fine white hairlines

TIGER ONYX.visual_description: A warm tan-honey onyx with strongly horizontal 'tiger-stripe' banding — alternating darker amber and lighter cream-honey bands flowing across the slab like wood grain or tiger fur. The pattern direction is the hallmark: if banded horizontally in this amber palette, it is Tiger Onyx. Translucent enough to backlight but less saturated than Honey Onyx in the base tone.
TIGER ONYX.differentiator: Strongly horizontal tiger-stripe banding is the key ID — Honey Onyx is cloud/cream patches (not bands), Mango is pebble/bubble cells (not bands), Noche Travertino is horizontal-striped too but matte rustic travertine not translucent onyx. If it's banded horizontally AND translucent AND amber-honey, it's Tiger Onyx.

pattern.type: horizontal wood-grain banding
pattern.vein_color: warm amber, caramel, dark tobacco, cream hairlines

TOBACCO BROWN.visual_description: A deep tobacco-brown onyx (often sold as quartzite or marble) with strongly directional horizontal wood-grain banding in alternating tobacco-brown and warm caramel-amber tones, interrupted by fine cream hairlines. The overall read is warm, rich, and woody — the quintessential 'tobacco' stone. Unlike Indian Tobacco (which is dark-grey with tobacco warmth), this is a true rich-brown.
TOBACCO BROWN.differentiator: True warm-brown wood-grain banding (not grey like Indian Tobacco, not chocolate-blotchy like Dark Emperador). The strongly horizontal banding is the hallmark. Among the warmest/richest browns in the family.

color.accent: pale pink-cream banded arcs and darker rust shadows

pattern.type: concentric fiery banded arcs with yellow-gold clusters
pattern.vein_color: fiery orange-red, warm yellow, pink-cream, rust-brown

TRAMONTO.visual_description: A dramatic fiery orange-red quartzite with concentric banded arcs sweeping across the slab — like a sunset ('tramonto' in Italian) painted across stone. Warm yellow-gold clusters interrupt the orange field, and pale pink-cream bands trace the arc direction. More fully saturated across the whole slab than Fuego (which splits hot and cool), and more arced-banded than Red Alikante (which is crackle-veined).
TRAMONTO.differentiator: Concentric sunset-arc banding with yellow-gold interruptions is unique — Fuego splits into two zones (orange + white), Red Alikante has white crackle (not yellow). If the slab looks like a painted sunset arc with orange + yellow, it's Tramonto.

color.secondary: diagonal lighter green and cream bands
color.accent: warm rust filaments and fine white hairlines

pattern.type: soft teal-green base with diagonal lighter green and cream banding and rust filaments
pattern.vein_color: lighter green, cream, warm rust, fine white

TROPICAL.visual_description: A soft teal-green quartzite with strong diagonal lighter green and cream banding and warm rust filaments threading across. Tropical aqua-green feel with directional character. Sister to Botanic and Aqua Patagonia Extra.
TROPICAL.differentiator: Soft teal-green with diagonal banding and rust filaments — lighter and more banded than Botanic (which has fracture lines), warmer accents than Aqua Patagonia Extra.

pattern.type: dense cream lattice / net veining across a dark brown field
pattern.vein_density: dense — full-coverage branching net of cream veins

TROPICAL STORM.visual_description: A dramatic dark chocolate-brown marble overlaid with a dense lattice/net of pale cream and beige veining that spreads across the slab like a storm-front over brown land — the namesake effect. Much more vein-dense than Dark Emperador, and far darker than Fantasy Brown. The cream net is the hero pattern; the brown field is the dramatic base.
TROPICAL STORM.differentiator: Cream net/lattice veining against chocolate brown is the signature — denser and more connected than Dark Emperador's individual hairlines, and lighter cream (not pure white) compared to French Brown's bright crackle. The veining dominates visually almost as much as the brown base.

pattern.type: bright white field with dense black crackle vein network
pattern.vein_density: very dense — full-coverage black crackle network

TWILIGHT.visual_description: A bright white marble with a dense network of black crackle veins spreading across the slab — high-contrast monochrome. Sister character to Grigio Fusion / Calacatta Black but INVERTED (white base with black crackle instead of black base with white crackle).
TWILIGHT.differentiator: Bright WHITE base with dense black crackle — INVERTED tonal dominance vs Grigio Fusion (black base with white crackle). Pattern type is similar; tonal dominance is flipped. Lens should note this as a pattern-adjacent / tone-inverted pairing.

color.accent: warm gold filament veining and dark mineral flecks

pattern.type: pale pink cloud-swirls on cream crystalline base with gold filament veining
pattern.vein_color: warm gold, dark mineral fleck, occasional dusty pink shadow
pattern.vein_density: low-medium — quiet cloud movement with sparse gold filaments

VALLE ROSSA.visual_description: A soft pale rose / dusty pink quartzite with flowing pink cloud-swirls drifting across a cream-white crystalline base, traced by warm gold filament veins. The pink is pastel and cool-warm mixed — not saturated — reading almost like rose-quartz. Elegant, understated, bridge between Pinks and Cream-Ivory.
VALLE ROSSA.differentiator: Palest pink in the group — more rose-quartz than pink-marble. Quartzite crystalline body (not marble) with gold filament accents. Pink Valencia has salmon crackle (Valle Rossa is cloudier), Pink Onyx has a single orange band (Valle Rossa is uniform pink), Ancora is plum-purple (much darker).

color.secondary: vibrant lime-green and olive-green painterly swirls
color.accent: darker charcoal crackle filaments and warm tan patches

pattern.type: white base with dramatic lime-green painterly swirls and fine dark crackle
pattern.vein_color: vibrant lime-green, darker olive, fine charcoal crackle, warm tan
pattern.vein_thickness: variable (broad painterly swirls and fine filaments)
pattern.vein_density: medium — full-coverage painterly movement on a white-dominant base

VERDE FUSION.visual_description: A dramatic white-cream quartzite with vibrant lime-green and olive-green painterly swirls sweeping across the slab like fresh green brushstrokes on pale canvas. Fine darker charcoal crackle filaments cut through for detail, and occasional warm tan patches add earthy contrast. The lime-green is saturated and spring-bright — a very distinctive fresh-green look.
VERDE FUSION.differentiator: White base with bright LIME-green swirls is the ID — Verde Patagonia has jagged dark green fracture zones (not swirls), Emerald Flame has copper + teal (no lime), Emerald Harmony is uniformly pale sage (no swirls). If the base is white-cream with vibrant lime/olive swirls, it's Verde Fusion.

color.accent: cream crystalline clusters and darker grey shadow zones

pattern.type: cool grey-white field with dramatic gold/rust diagonal veining and cream crystalline accents
pattern.vein_color: warm gold, rust, darker grey shadow, fine white
pattern.vein_density: medium — diagonal gold vein pattern across a cool grey base

VERDE KARZAI.visual_description: A cool grey-white marble with dramatic gold and rust diagonal veining threaded across the slab, interrupted by cream crystalline clusters and darker grey shadow zones. Despite 'Verde' name, visually reads as a cool grey marble with warm gold accents — NOT green. Similar warm-cool contrast character to Azulado (in Blues family).
VERDE KARZAI.differentiator: Cool grey-white with dramatic gold diagonal veins — NOT visually green. Similar to Azulado but grey-dominant (not blue-grey) with gold instead of rust. The warm-cool contrast from gold veining is the hallmark.

color.accent: warm rust-brown and amber diagonal vein clusters

pattern.type: pale green onyx field with flowing cream patches and warm rust diagonal vein clusters
pattern.vein_color: warm rust-brown, amber, cream, occasional dark shadow
pattern.vein_thickness: variable (broad vein clusters and fine filaments)
pattern.vein_density: medium — flowing movement with warm accent vein clusters on a pale green base

VERDE ONYX.visual_description: A translucent onyx with a pale celadon/sage green field, interrupted by soft cream flowing patches and warm rust-brown / amber diagonal vein clusters that bring earthy warmth to the cool green base. The only true onyx in the Greens family — backlit-capable. The warm-cool contrast between the green field and the rust accents is the visual signature.
VERDE ONYX.differentiator: Only TRANSLUCENT onyx in the Greens family — all other Greens are opaque quartzites or semi-precious stones. Pale green with warm rust-brown/amber accents. Backlit applications showcase this stone uniquely.

color.secondary: bright white crystalline matrix / vein network
color.accent: occasional rust-red and fine dark crackle

pattern.type: large angular teal-green fracture zones separated by bright white crystalline matrix
pattern.vein_color: bright white, rust-red, dark charcoal filaments
pattern.vein_thickness: medium to broad (white matrix between fractures)
pattern.vein_density: medium-dense — angular fracture pattern with prominent white matrix

VERDE PATAGONIA EXTRA.visual_description: A dramatic quartzite where large angular teal-green fracture zones are separated by a bold bright-white crystalline matrix, like stained-glass panes of green separated by white leading. Occasional rust-red and fine dark crackle filaments add detail. The fracture pattern is the hero — jagged geometric shapes of green on white, unlike any other Green in the collection.
VERDE PATAGONIA EXTRA.differentiator: Visually VERY similar to Aqua Patagonia Extra (which sits in Blues family) — both are Patagonia quartzites with teal-green fracture zones on white matrix. Verde Patagonia Extra tends to read slightly greener/less teal; Aqua Patagonia Extra tends to read more teal-blue. Lens should expect heavy cross-family confusion between Verde Patagonia Extra (Greens) and Aqua Patagonia Extra (Blues) — the two are trade-separated variants of the same Patagonia quartzite family.

color.secondary: dense bright white crackle vein network

pattern.type: very dark forest-green base with dense bright-white crackle vein network
pattern.vein_color: bright white (dense branching crackle), occasional olive-green highlight
pattern.vein_density: dense — full-coverage branching white crackle across a dark green base

VERDE VERMONT.visual_description: A very dark forest-green marble (reads almost black at distance) with a dense network of bright white crackle veins spreading across the slab — the classic 'Vermont green' look. The white veining nearly equals the green in visual weight, creating a strong high-contrast pattern. Deeper and darker than Avocado, denser veining than Avocatus. The darkest Green in the family.
VERDE VERMONT.differentiator: Darkest Green in the family — reads almost black with dense bright white crackle. Avocado is deeper-green with crisp white veins (less dense crackle), Avocatus has grey-green painterly swirls (not crackle). If the slab is near-black with web-like white crackle, it's Verde Vermont.

color.accent: gold and bronze filaments, bright white crystalline streaks

pattern.type: horizontal wavy banding with iridescent blue, grey-green, gold streaks
pattern.vein_color: iridescent blue, grey-green, bronze-gold, bright white crystalline
pattern.vein_thickness: variable (broad wavy bands and fine filaments)
pattern.vein_density: dense — full-coverage horizontal wavy movement across the slab

VIBRANIUM.visual_description: A dramatic dark-blue Brazilian quartzite with strong horizontal wavy banding — deep iridescent blue meeting grey-green swirls, cut through with bronze-gold filaments and bright white crystalline streaks. The direction is the hallmark: wave-like, flowing left-to-right, like stormy sea. Completely different character from Lazurite or Sodalite — no pyrite flecks, no uniform blue field, instead a moving, directional, multi-tonal composition.
VIBRANIUM.differentiator: Horizontal wavy banding in dark iridescent blue with bronze-gold streaks is unique in Blues — NOT similar to Lazurite/Sodalite (which are static flecked royal-blue fields with no directional movement). Also distinct from Lemurian (labradorite granite with blue flash in a dark crystalline matrix, not horizontal waves). If the slab looks like a stormy sea in motion, it's Vibranium.

pattern.type: near-solid

VIETNAM WHITE.visual_description: A bright, uniform white marble from Vietnam with virtually no visible veining. Reads as a near-solid white plane with a very faint warm glow. Clean, commercial, and consistent — an affordable alternative to Thassos for volume applications.
VIETNAM WHITE.differentiator: Slightly warmer undertone than pure Thassos, but cooler and cleaner than Dior Pearl's pearl glow. Not quite as glacially pure as Thassos but nearly as uniform. Typically used when the project needs a pure-white look at volume.

pattern.type: branching veined

WHITE ONYX.visual_description: A translucent pearly white onyx with a dramatic branching network of rust-orange and amber veining spreading across the slab like roots or capillaries. Soft cream pooling fills the negative space. Best revealed backlit, where the crystalline translucency glows and the rust veins become luminous.
WHITE ONYX.differentiator: True translucent onyx with vivid rust-orange vein network — much warmer and more dramatic than Crystal Yellow Onyx which is pale and subtle. Shares the rust color with Bianco Eliptus but White Onyx has organic branching veins vs Eliptus's sharp angular fractures, and White Onyx has crystalline translucency marble lacks. Ideal backlit application stone.

color.accent: warm rust hairline veins and subtle tan undertones

pattern.type: soft cool grey mottling with occasional rust hairline accents
pattern.vein_color: warm rust, fine white, darker grey mottle
pattern.vein_density: low — quiet mottled field with sparse rust accents

ZEBRANO.visual_description: A light cool grey travertine with soft natural mottling and occasional warm rust hairline veins threading through. Quieter and more neutral than Silver Travertino (which has stronger horizontal banding), more grey than Beige Travertino. Despite 'Zebrano' name (suggesting zebra-stripes), the pattern is mottled rather than striped.
ZEBRANO.differentiator: Lighter cool grey travertine with soft mottling and sparse rust accents — quieter than Silver Travertino's strong bands. Name suggests stripes but pattern is mottled.
